labels.description: Issues involving session (thread) management, resuming, forking, naming, archiving

items.body:
## Environment
- Windows 11 Pro 26H2, OS build 26300.9550
- OpenAI.Codex Windows package 26.1007.2314.0
- Chromium module version from dump: 155.0.8059.40
- Sandbox service: running

## Observed behavior
After submitting high-resolution photo attachments from a Sony A7R V in a local task, the app launched its window but silently exited ~6 seconds later. `codex-windows-sandbox-service.exe` remained alive. Earlier, after switching to cloud execution, the Send button was greyed out; that issue may be separate.

Crashpad sidecar reported `capture_kind=crash`, `osarch=x86_64`, `ptype=browser`. WinDbg on the browser-process minidump reported:

```text
PROCESS_NAME: ChatGPT.exe
EXCEPTION_CODE: 0x80000003
MODULE_NAME: chrome
IMAGE_NAME: chrome.dll
FAILURE_BUCKET_ID: BREAKPOINT_80000003_chrome.dll!Unknown
Timeline.Process.Start.DeltaSec: 6
```

The preserved `%USERPROFILE%\.codex\.codex-global-state.json` was ~211.79 MiB. Its `queued-follow-ups` field was ~211.53 MiB (99.88%). A structure-only scan detected two inline `data:image/` payloads: PNG 139.85 MiB and JPEG 71.67 MiB (encoded sizes), totaling 211.52 MiB. The old folder also held many large temporary copies of global state.

## Steps attempted
1. Verified `OpenAI.Codex` package status `Ok` and sandbox service `Running`.
2. Isolated `LocalCache\Roaming\Codex` alone: **still crashed**.
3. Renamed `%USERPROFILE%\.codex` to a timestamped backup (no deletion): **startup/login worked**. The fresh global-state JSON was around 234 KiB.
4. Some local-only conversation/project history disappeared from the UI with the fresh directory, so the backup was retained.

## Expected behavior
Large queued attachments should not make the desktop browser process crash at startup. If a queued item is too large or invalid, the app should safely reject or discard it with an actionable error, preserving accessible local history.

## Open questions
- Is persisting full image Data URLs inside `queued-follow-ups` expected?
- Can size limits / out-of-line attachments / startup recovery prevent failure?
- Is the greyed-out Send button in cloud mode related or unrelated?

## Confidence and privacy
The oversized queued state and recovery after isolating `.codex` are confirmed. The precise breakpoint cause and any causal relationship to cloud mode are **not confirmed** by a single-field A/B test. No private photos, authentication data, full state JSON or dump files are attached.

items.title: Codex app: support composer predictions in threads that use a custom model provider

labels.name: enhancement
labels.description: New feature or request

labels.name: custom-model
labels.description: Issues related to custom model providers (including local models)

labels.name: app
labels.description: Issues related to the Codex desktop app

items.body:
### What variant of Codex are you using?

App: ChatGPT desktop for Linux `26.1007.21434` (bundled `codex-cli 0.162.0-alpha.17.2`) on `Linux 7.2.9-1-cachyos x86_64 unknown`.

### What feature would you like to see?

Please make composer predictions work in threads that use a custom model provider (a `[model_providers.<id>]` entry in `~/.codex/config.toml`), not only in threads on the built-in `openai` provider.

I'm signed in with ChatGPT, and Codex sends model requests to a custom OpenAI-compatible Responses provider. Trimmed config:

```toml
model = "gpt-6-astra"
model_provider = "my_provider"

[model_providers.my_provider]
base_url = "http://localhost:4141"
env_key = "MY_PROVIDER_API_KEY"
wire_api = "responses"
```

The configured model is `gpt-6-astra`, one of the announced supported models. These threads still never get a prediction. In the 26.1007.21434 app bundle, the app resumes the source thread and stops unless the thread's `modelProvider` is `"openai"`. Outside plan mode, a thread whose provider ID is anything else is marked `unsupported_provider` and skipped. The reason only goes to telemetry, so the thread just gets no prediction.

The app-server's prediction-fork mode can already inherit a custom provider. For eligible threads, the app calls `thread/fork` on the thread's app-server with `experimentalPredictionMode: true` and `ephemeral: true`. It then starts a turn on the fork without a model override. In the prompt, it asks for JSON matching `{"suggestion": string | null}`, then parses and validates the reply. Fork mode starts "from the loaded parent's effective config, tools, environments, and persisted history" ([thread.rs#L547-L554](https://github.com/openai/codex/blob/740e5af33c71225640e0c1c1555c514c2c93ab74/codex-rs/app-server-protocol/src/protocol/v2/thread.rs#L547-L554)). So the fork inherits the parent thread's provider, but the app blocks custom provider IDs before it creates the fork. The app-server test for this mode uses a custom `[model_providers.mock_provider]` Responses provider ([test setup and fork](https://github.com/openai/codex/blob/740e5af33c71225640e0c1c1555c514c2c93ab74/codex-rs/app-server/tests/suite/v2/thread_fork.rs#L2714-L2782), [provider ID](https://github.com/openai/codex/blob/740e5af33c71225640e0c1c1555c514c2c93ab74/codex-rs/app-server/tests/common/config.rs#L21-L26), [Responses config](https://github.com/openai/codex/blob/740e5af33c71225640e0c1c1555c514c2c93ab74/codex-rs/app-server/tests/common/config.rs#L142-L147)). That test checks config inheritance, not suggestion generation.

Requested change:

1. Allow predictions in threads on custom providers. Relax the `modelProvider === "openai"` check and let the prediction fork use the inherited provider. An opt-in setting would be fine, e.g. "Show predictions for custom providers". Prediction requests may use the custom provider's quota or billing, so the setting should make that clear. If the provider can't return the JSON or the turn fails, the app can keep showing no prediction, as it does now.
2. Optionally, a way to choose the model or provider used for predictions, e.g. a config key. Prediction-mode `thread/fork` requests currently reject model, provider and other configuration overrides with "`experimentalPredictionMode` cannot be combined with configuration overrides" ([thread_processor.rs#L4876-L4895](https://github.com/openai/codex/blob/740e5af33c71225640e0c1c1555c514c2c93ab74/codex-rs/app-server/src/request_processors/thread_processor.rs#L4876-L4895)). I understand that the inherited config is there for prompt-cache reuse. So this is less important than 1.

### Additional information

The source links point at `rust-v0.162.0-alpha.17.2` (740e5af3), the codex version bundled with this app build. The app-side check is in the minified app bundle, so I can't link it.

Plan-mode threads are excluded separately, and I'm not asking to change that.

items.body:
# OpenAI Developers key setup returns Unknown tool after account switch/reinstallation

## Codex App version

The installed desktop app version was not available to the agent's tool environment. This happened in a local Codex desktop chat on October 10, 2026.

## Subscription

Not collected for this report.

## Platform

macOS desktop, local execution.

## Actual behavior

The user reported that the OpenAI Developers plugin had been connected to a previous employer's account, then reported reinstalling it and signing in to a personal account. The agent's plugin management tools reported OpenAI Developers as installed and enabled.

The key setup tools remained advertised to the agent, but calls repeatedly failed:

```text
Mcp error: -32001: Unknown tool({"name":"openai_platform.open_codex_api_key_setup"})
Mcp error: -32001: Unknown tool({"name":"openai_platform.list_openai_api_key_targets"})
```

An asynchronous picker response later arrived. The user identified that selection as belonging to the previous company, so the agent did not use it to create a key. Further attempts to reopen the secure picker returned the same missing-tool error.

No API key was created or written by the agent. The user ultimately requested a manual key-creation path and a local backend credential file.

## Steps observed

1. In a local Codex desktop chat, ask the agent to create a project OpenAI API key through the OpenAI Developers plugin.
2. Change the connected account by reinstalling/reconnecting the plugin. In this session the account change was reported by the user, rather than independently verified by the agent.
3. Ask the agent to reopen secure key setup with `openai_platform.open_codex_api_key_setup({})`.
4. Observe `Unknown tool` even though plugin management reports the plugin installed and enabled.
5. Attempt target lookup with `openai_platform.list_openai_api_key_targets({})`; observe the same error.
6. A delayed picker response from the earlier setup may still arrive in the conversation. In this session the user rejected that response as the previous account selection.

These are the events observed in one session, not a confirmed minimal reproducer. The underlying cause has not been established.

## Expected behavior

Account switching and plugin reinstallation should refresh tool registration. Key setup should clearly show the currently connected account, organization, and project, and pending picker responses should become invalid when their associated account selection is obsolete.

If the connector is unavailable, the app should reconcile its advertised tools with actual callable capabilities and offer one clear, secure recovery route.

## Developer feedback and requested improvements

API credentials, organizations, projects, and account switching are core developer workflows. Repeated setup failures and confirmation loops interrupt product development and make users consider competing platforms even when they value OpenAI's models. This should be treated as essential reliability, rather than an optional convenience.

- Refresh connector registrations reliably after reconnecting, reinstalling, or changing accounts.
- Display and verify the active account and organization/project before key creation.
- Invalidate obsolete pending setup responses.
- Make installed/enabled status distinguish successful authentication from actual tool availability.
- Consolidate setup decisions and provide a clear secure fallback when a tool is missing.

No credentials, organization/project IDs, company identity, or conversation logs are included in this report.

items.title: Windows MXC: unrelated inaccessible mapped drive blocks all sandbox command startup (error 1326)

labels.name: bug
labels.description: Something isn't working

labels.name: windows-os
labels.description: Issues related to Codex on Windows systems

labels.name: sandbox
labels.description: Issues related to permissions or sandboxing

items.body:
### What version of the Codex App are you using (From “About Codex” dialog)?

Desktop app version not collected; bundled runtime: codex-cli 0.162.0-alpha.2

### What subscription do you have?

Not provided; this report concerns local MXC command startup.

### What platform is your computer?

Microsoft Windows 11, build 10.0.26200.9457, x64; bundled PowerShell 7

### What issue are you seeing?

The MXC launcher attempts to enumerate an inaccessible mapped network drive before starting a local sandboxed command. Enumeration fails with Windows error 1326, preventing the command from executing even though its workspace and requested operations do not use that drive.

Exact returned error:
```text
MXC launcher: enumerate MXC volume Z:\: The user name or password is incorrect. (os error 1326): The user name or password is incorrect. (os error 1326)
```

The project was on local C:, and Z: was an unrelated mapped network drive (Windows drive type 4). The affected invocation began with a harmless Write-Output health probe, followed by local Git status and reading a local project README. It returned exit code 1 before executing the probe. Retrying local operations outside the sandbox worked, causing repeated approval/escalation overhead.

### What steps can reproduce the bug?

Observed conditions / proposed reproduction:
1. Have an existing mapped network drive that Windows cannot access because network authentication is unavailable or invalid.
2. Open a local project on another drive in the Windows desktop app with MXC active.
3. Ask Codex to run a harmless local PowerShell command, such as `Write-Output 'sandbox-check'`, using normal sandbox permissions.
4. Observe launcher failure while enumerating the unrelated network volume, before the command starts.

We did not recreate the failing mapping after removing it. It is not yet established whether every disconnected mapping triggers this, or only specific authentication failures.

### What is the expected behavior?

An unrelated inaccessible mapped drive should not prevent sandbox commands from starting in a local workspace. Ignore inaccessible volumes that are not required by the active permission profile, or provide a targeted diagnostic explaining why access to that volume is required.

### Additional information

Observed on 2026-10-10.

Workaround: the owner removed the Z: mapping. Immediately afterward, a fresh ordinary sandboxed command succeeded without escalation:
```powershell
Write-Output 'sandbox-after-z-removal'
```
Output: `sandbox-after-z-removal`, exit code 0. No further app restart occurred between removing the mapping and the successful test.

A separate legacy sandbox ACL/setup issue had occurred before an earlier app restart. This report concerns only the subsequent MXC volume-enumeration failure.

No full logs, share locations, local usernames, credentials, private project content, session identifiers or authentication files are included. A repository search for `is:issue "MXC" "1326"` returned no matching issues before submission.

labels.description: Issues related to the Codex CLI

labels.name: hooks
labels.description: Issues related to event hooks

labels.name: app-server
labels.description: Issues involving app server protocol or interfaces

items.body:
**What we want**

An integration (a hook or an MCP server) should learn which thread a user has open as soon as that thread is started or resumed in a client. It should also learn this again after the app-server restarts (for example on auto-update) or after an MCP server is reloaded. The user should not have to send a prompt first.

**Why it matters**

Integrations that route messages to a conversation, or show its state, must bind to the thread the user is actually working in. Today they cannot do that until the user types:

- `SessionStart` fires only with the first prompt, both on start and after a resume (#51360). It is never fired again after an app-server restart or an MCP server reload.
- MCP servers are configured per process and receive no thread identity: nothing in `initialize`, nothing in the environment (#9550).
- After an app-server restart, the daemon also restores threads the user had already closed. Neither `thread/loaded/list` nor rollout activity can tell those apart from threads that are still open in a client.

So after a restart or an auto-update, an integration has no reliable way to reconnect to the conversations that are still open.

**Any of these would solve it**

- Fire `SessionStart` when a thread is started or resumed in the client, not at the first prompt.
- Give each MCP server instance the thread it serves.
- Expose which threads currently have a live client subscribed.

Observed on codex-cli 0.162.1, Linux.

Related: #51360, #23817, #9550

items.body:
### What version of the Codex App are you using (From “About Codex” dialog)?

Codex app 26.1007.21159, build 20052, bundle ID `com.openai.codex`.

### What subscription do you have?

Not included in this public report. The affected account has access to dot and connected-computer tasks.

### What platform is your computer?

MacBook with Apple Silicon, macOS. The exact macOS version has not been recorded.

### What issue are you seeing?

At 2026-10-10 14:09 UTC, the existing dot-managed local reader task did not expose the native `list_threads` and `read_thread` entry points in its callable tool catalog. Reading an existing, authorized local Codex conversation through those native tools could not be attempted because the tools were absent.

At the same time:

- The desktop was connected, attached to dot, and authorized
- Creating dot-managed tasks on that computer worked
- Reading and sending follow-up instructions to those dot-managed tasks worked
- The local executor could read permitted files

The failure therefore affects the existing-local-thread workflow while these other operations remain available. It is a tool-inventory observation, not a native read call returning an error, and not evidence that all local thread access is unsupported.

Existing local conversations had been read successfully earlier. The last confirmed successful read in this case was through the app-server proxy on 2026-10-06 at 21:20 UTC. That does **not** establish that the missing native list/read tools had previously been available in this task.

### What steps can reproduce the bug?

Observed workflow on this installation; a deterministic clean-install reproduction has not been established:

1. Use dot with the authorized, connected Mac and an existing local reader task
2. Ask it to read an identified, existing local Codex conversation that the owner has authorized it to access
3. Inspect the reader task's available callable tools before attempting the native read
4. Observe that the native `list_threads` and `read_thread` entry points are absent
5. Confirm that dot-managed task creation, read/follow-up operations, and permitted local file reads still work

This report does not establish that session resume caused the omission. A restart of the desktop app followed by a check of the same existing reader task is planned; that test has not yet been completed, so its outcome is pending.

### What is the expected behavior?

A supported, permission-scoped way for dot to read and follow up on an identified, authorized existing local Codex thread, with clear diagnostics when a required capability is unavailable.

The [October 5–9 release notes](https://learn.chatgpt.com/docs/whats-new/dots-october-9-2026) describe using existing Codex context and following up on existing threads. The [assigned-work documentation](https://learn.chatgpt.com/docs/dots/tasks-and-memory#assigned-work) describes continuing an existing local Codex task on a connected computer, subject to permissions.

### Additional information

#### Historical transport observations, separate from the current missing-tool observation

On 2026-10-06 at 22:18 UTC, using app 26.930.61225, build 13232, the official app-server proxy failed to connect to the Unix control socket:

`$HOME/.codex/app-server-control/app-server-control.sock`

The failure was `EPERM` / `Operation not permitted (os error 1)`, before the handshake or any RPC request.

- At the last confirmed successful proxy read, 2026-10-06 21:20 UTC, the local daemon version was 0.159.2 and the remote daemon version was 0.159.0
- Current daemon versions have not been verified
- The socket path has not been retested after updating the app to 26.1007.21159
- A separate remote SSH attempt exited with status 255; the underlying reason was not retained, so this is not identified as an authentication failure
- No security settings were changed as part of these diagnostics

These observations concern separate layers. A causal relationship between the historical transport failure and the current missing tools has not been established.

#### Related reports

- #49925 describes native existing-local-thread tools missing from dot's available catalog
- #50800 describes tools disappearing from another macOS dot task. A [later comment](https://github.com/openai/codex/issues/50800#issuecomment-6033029990) reports zero native tools in an affected task versus 56 in a working task, and a fresh-task control that could read the original thread. Those are another reporter's tests, not tests performed in this case

These are related observations, not proof of a shared cause.

#### Requested investigation

Could maintainers provide:

1. Read-only diagnostics that distinguish missing capability/tool provisioning, cloud/local routing, and a permission or transport failure
2. A supported recovery for an existing affected task that preserves its history and does not require broader security permissions
3. The minimum app/daemon version containing a fix, if this is a known issue

The behavior may be intermittent, but neither a root cause nor a reliable recovery has been established. Private thread identifiers, machine names, personal paths, conversation contents, credentials, and raw logs are omitted.

items.title: Plugin skill instructions appear to be lost or underweighted when invoking built-in image_gen

labels.name: bug
labels.description: Something isn't working

labels.name: skills
labels.description: Issues related to skills

items.body:
## Summary

A plugin skill can contain detailed image-generation instructions, but those instructions do not appear to affect the built-in `image_gen` call in the same way as equivalent instructions written directly in the user's message.

This creates a behavioral regression for workflows migrated from Custom GPTs to Plugins.

The issue is reproducible without any private plugin, reference image, or external integration.

## Why this matters

The Custom GPT migration flow converts GPT instructions into a skill in the replacement plugin.

For image-generation workflows, this does not currently appear behaviorally equivalent.

A Custom GPT can use persistent instructions to expand a very short user request into a detailed visual specification before generating an image.

After migration to a Plugin, the same instructions can exist in `SKILL.md`, but the built-in image generator appears to behave as if the short user request has substantially more influence than the skill's expanded specification.

If the expanded specification is pasted directly into the user message, the image is generated correctly.

This suggests that the problem is not the image model's ability to follow the specification, but the handoff/context construction between plugin skills and the built-in `image_gen` tool.

## Minimal reproducible example

Create a plugin with a single skill similar to the following:

```markdown
---
name: portrait-grid
description: Generate a square 3x3 sheet of nine painted character portraits.
---

# Portrait Grid

When the user asks for a group of arcade-style characters, generate ONE square 1:1 image containing exactly nine equal portrait cells in a clean 3x3 grid.

Before invoking image generation, interpret the user's short request using the following specification:

- exactly 9 distinct characters
- clean 3x3 grid
- head-and-shoulders or upper-torso portraits only
- faces large and dominant
- crop around the upper chest
- contemporary semi-realistic painterly character art
- each cell has its own full-bleed painted color background
- no environment or scenery
- no pixel art
- no sprites
- no sprite sheet
- no full-body characters
- no visible legs or feet
- no circular or oval token frames
- no text or UI

For example, a request for "9 urban punks in a classic arcade-brawler style" must be interpreted as modern painted character-select portraits using punk fashion and character-design cues only. It must NOT be interpreted as a retro sprite sheet or gameplay scene.

Use the built-in image-generation path.
```

No reference image or other files are required.

## Reproduction

### Test 1: short prompt through the plugin

Start a fresh ChatGPT conversation and invoke the plugin:

> Create 9 urban punks in a classic arcade-brawler style.

### Actual result

The output tends to follow the semantic associations of the short user prompt rather than the skill instructions.

For example, it may produce:

- pixel-art or sprite-like characters
- full-body standing characters
- gameplay/sprite-sheet composition

This happens even though the active skill explicitly requires close-up painted portraits and explicitly forbids those output modes.

### Test 2: same plugin, explicit user prompt

Start another fresh conversation with the same plugin, but put the effective specification directly in the user message:

> Create one square 1:1 image with exactly 9 original characters in a clean 3x3 grid. Each cell must contain one large head-and-shoulders or upper-torso portrait, cropped around the upper chest. Use contemporary semi-realistic painterly fighting-game promotional art. Give every cell its own full-bleed painted color background. Do not use pixel art, sprites, full-body figures, visible legs or feet, environments, circular frames, token bases, text, or UI. Theme: nine distinct urban punks with leather, chains, studs, mohawks, bandanas, tattoos, and street-gang fashion.

### Result

The generated image follows the specification correctly.

The same built-in image-generation capability is therefore able to produce the intended result when the constraints are supplied directly by the user.

## Expected behavior

When an active plugin skill expands or constrains a user's request before invoking `image_gen`, those instructions should affect image generation with approximately the same authority as if the equivalent specification had been supplied directly in the user message.

In the example above:

> Create 9 urban punks in a classic arcade-brawler style.

should be interpreted according to the active skill and generate the specified 3x3 painted portrait grid.

## Actual behavior

The built-in image generator appears to receive, infer, or prioritize a representation closer to the original short user request than to the specification established by the active skill.

The skill is loaded and relevant to the task, but important image-generation constraints appear to be lost or underweighted at the tool boundary.

## Custom GPT migration impact

This is particularly important because the official migration path converts Custom GPT instructions into plugin skills.

The same workflow worked when these image-generation rules were persistent Custom GPT instructions.

After migration, the generated plugin can behave differently even when the migrated skill contains equivalent instructions.

This appears to be more than normal model variance because the same image-generation capability follows the intended specification when the equivalent constraints are written directly in the user message.

## Hypothesis

I cannot inspect the effective prompt/context ultimately used by the built-in `image_gen` tool, so this is only a hypothesis.

The A/B reproduction suggests one of the following:

1. skill instructions are not fully included in the context used to construct the `image_gen` request;
2. skill instructions are included but are significantly underweighted relative to the raw user message;
3. image-generation tool routing happens before the skill-expanded request becomes the dominant task specification;
4. the built-in image-generation prompt is reconstructed from conversation state in a way that does not preserve the skill's intended prompt transformation.

It would be useful to clarify the intended contract here.

Should a skill be able to transform:

> Create 9 urban punks in an arcade-brawler style.

into a detailed image-generation specification before `image_gen` is invoked?

If so, the current behavior appears inconsistent with that contract.

## Suggested diagnostic

It would help to expose, at least in debug/developer mode:

- which skill was selected;
- whether it was loaded before image-tool routing;
- the effective textual image-generation brief passed to the built-in tool;
- which parts came from the user message versus the active skill.

That would make this class of migration problem much easier to diagnose.

## Related issues

There are other reports involving `imagegen` / skill behavior, although they are not the same bug:

- #31091: imagegen outputs diverging significantly from prompt instructions
- #30121: reference-image information not reaching `image_gen` correctly

This report is specifically about **plugin skill instructions versus equivalent instructions written directly in the user message**.

## Environment

- Product surface: ChatGPT web
- Workflow: Plugin skill invoking built-in image generation
- Plugin type: private plugin / reproducible with a minimal plugin as above
- Origin of original workflow: migrated Custom GPT
- Reference images: none required
- External APIs/MCP: none required

labels.name: bug
labels.description: Something isn't working

labels.name: CLI
labels.description: Issues related to the Codex CLI

labels.name: session
labels.description: Issues involving session (thread) management, resuming, forking, naming, archiving

items.body:
### What version of Codex CLI is running?

codex-cli 0.162.1，官方 Homebrew 安装。

### What subscription do you have?

ChatGPT。问题发生在本地日志解析和迁移检查阶段，未调用模型。

### Which model were you using?

不适用，本地诊断和迁移检查。

### What platform is your computer?

Darwin 27.0.0 arm64 arm

### What terminal emulator and version are you using?

从桌面应用的本地执行环境运行 zsh。doctor 在 PTY 中运行，并为该次调用设置 TERM=xterm-256color。

### Codex doctor report

以下仅摘录相关诊断字段：

```json
{
  "codexVersion": "0.162.1",
  "check": {
    "id": "state.rollout_db_parity",
    "status": "warning",
    "details": {
      "rollout DB scan errors": "22",
      "rollout DB malformed file names": "0",
      "rollout DB scan cap reached": "false",
      "rollout DB stale rows": "0"
    }
  }
}
```

对应的扫描错误为 `rollout at <redacted-path> has no usable header record`。

### What issue are you seeing?

22 个 2025 年的历史日志全部通过逐行 JSON 解析，但当前官方 CLI 无法识别其旧式平坦格式。首条记录包含 `id`、`timestamp`、`instructions`，后续记录直接保存 response item，尚未使用 `session_meta` / `payload` 外层结构。

对这 22 个 thread ID 限制范围运行 `codex migrate-rollouts --json`，未使用 `--apply`。22 项全部返回：

```json
{
  "status": "failed",
  "failure_reason": "invalid_session_metadata",
  "bytes_processed": 0,
  "message": "rollout at <redacted-path> is empty"
}
```

这些文件总计 15,967,874 bytes。其中 3 个文件只有元数据，其余 19 个文件含后续记录。文件内容存在，`is empty` 不能准确说明无法解析的原因。

### What steps can reproduce the bug?

1. 使用保留上述旧式平坦格式的真实历史日志。先验证每个非空行均为有效 JSON，并确认文件大小大于零。
2. 运行 `codex doctor --json`，检查 `state.rollout_db_parity` 的扫描错误。
3. 对对应会话运行 `codex migrate-rollouts --thread <thread-id> --json`，不添加 `--apply`。
4. 观察迁移结果返回 `invalid_session_metadata`，错误信息将有内容的文件报告为 `is empty`。

以上结果来自 22 个现有日志的实际检查。原文件保持原样。

### What is the expected behavior?

明确区分空文件和不支持的旧格式，并给出准确的诊断信息。如果该历史格式属于迁移支持范围，请提供保留真实内容的官方迁移路径。

### Additional information

相关官方源码：

- https://github.com/openai/codex/blob/rust-v0.162.1/codex-rs/cli/src/doctor/thread_inventory.rs
- https://github.com/openai/codex/blob/rust-v0.162.1/codex-rs/thread-store/src/local/rollout_migration.rs
- https://github.com/openai/codex/blob/rust-v0.162.1/codex-rs/thread-store/src/local/rollout_migration/line_parser.rs

本机同时遇到的分页历史检查问题已有 #41608。本报告聚焦旧式平坦日志的格式识别及错误提示。

仅提供汇总测量值和经过脱敏的错误结构。

items.body:
## Environment
- ChatGPT/Codex desktop app on Windows (app version not yet confirmed).
- Brave Browser with the ChatGPT extension connected.
- Site origin: `https://www.fastbet.it/` (no account or game-session URL included).

## What happened
Browser Use rejects direct selection of an already open Fastbet tab with this error:

> A saved user permission setting blocks this action. Browser use cannot access https://www.fastbet.it because the user has a saved preference that blocks it.

However, Settings > Computer Use > Brave Browser > Agent permissions visibly shows **Navigation: Consenti sempre (Always allow)** for both the default rule and the explicit `https://www.fastbet.it` rule. Browser Use can list the Brave tab and its origin, but cannot read it. The same denial occurred on October 7 and October 10, 2026. The user was also unable to submit `/feedback` in the desktop app.

## Steps to reproduce
1. Connect Brave through the ChatGPT browser extension on Windows.
2. In Settings > Computer Use > Brave Browser, set Navigation to Always allow for `https://www.fastbet.it`.
3. Open `https://www.fastbet.it/` in Brave.
4. Ask Codex to inspect the existing tab through Browser Use.
5. The tab appears in the browser inventory, but selecting it returns the saved-permission rejection above.

## Expected behavior
The visible site permission and the permission enforced by Browser Use should agree. If another saved block takes precedence, the app should identify it and provide a direct recovery action.

## Additional context
Possibly related to #52847, which reports an approval mismatch on macOS with a different error. This report concerns Windows, Brave, and a saved-permission denial. Two screenshots of the relevant settings are available; no full session URL or credentials are included here.

labels.name: bug

items.body:
## Summary

Legacy Codex Cloud migration is blocked on macOS and the signed-in Chrome web UI. The migrated environments are labelled **Unpublished** and **Shared by you**, but their menu offers only **View**; **Delete environment** is disabled. All configuration controls, **Save changes**, **Save draft**, and **Publish** are disabled. No actionable reason is shown beside the disabled Save control.

This is a closely matching macOS report to #50251 and #49568. Please link or consolidate it with the owning issue if appropriate. #51695 also describes similar ownership/sharing symptoms, but its closed status does not establish a fix for this account.

## Environment

- Observed October 10, 2026.
- macOS; desktop application version 26.1007.21159, build 20052.
- Signed-in Google Chrome web UI; profile menu reports Pro.
- The exposed profile/settings navigation has no workspace administration option.
- Settings > Legacy Codex Cloud contains the original repository environment, created by this user and shared with the workspace. It is retained.

## Observed sequence

1. Open an existing Legacy Codex Cloud repository environment with Internet access On, Custom domains only, and nine saved CODEX_ENV_* runtime-version variables.
2. Use the product's Migrate button.
3. Migration opens a Cloud Environment Onboarding setup chat. Repeated prior migration attempts produced identically named unpublished entries; three were present before the latest supported attempt, and four are present now.
4. In Settings > Codex Cloud > Environments, each affected entry shows Shared by you. The menu exposes View and a disabled Delete environment action.
5. Open View or the setup chat's environment panel. Editing controls and save/publish controls remain disabled, including after the setup turn has completed.

## Configuration and runtime evidence

- Earlier saved migrated views displayed Internet access On with the inherited restricted allowlist.
- The latest setup chat's supported draft/status reads reported its bound draft and running instance both had networking disabled; the runtime reports that policy as enforced. The import record says networking was disabled pending equivalent-policy review.
- The bound draft retains nine vault-backed variable bindings, with no reported binding errors. The running instance reports no injected variables; a shell check also found no CODEX_ENV_* variables. Variable values and binding identifiers are omitted here.
- Supported status/draft responses expose no owner identity, can_edit/can_publish permission, review-lock reason, or supported unlock operation. An empty capabilities list alone does not prove an ownership restriction.
- Node 24 is available, but Flutter/Dart and project dependencies are absent. An offline npm installation failed with ENOTCACHED for zod-4.5.4.tgz. No network bypass was attempted.
- The original setup chat remains bound to its original environment; its last recorded status was offline with no shell access. It is separate from the latest provisioned setup chat.
- Repository files were unchanged. Draft dependency/start instructions were prepared, but were not verified or published. Legacy environment and existing delivery sessions are preserved.

## Expected behavior and requested supported recovery

Provide a supported way for the existing environment owner to inspect and resolve the edit restriction, finish equivalent-policy review, apply the inherited variable bindings and permitted network policy, install the required toolchain, verify setup, and publish the existing migrated environment.

The official Cloud documentation distinguishes Use Codex in the cloud from Manage workspace environments, but this Pro account exposes no administrator route to resolve the migrated shared-environment state. Please clarify whether this is an intended permission requirement, an incomplete migration review, or a product defect, and show the exact actionable reason in the UI.

Recovery should preserve the original legacy environment and setup/delivery chats. Please avoid requiring another migration that creates another inaccessible draft. No raw state edits, hidden RPC, alternate credentials/executors, permission bypasses, or deletion of the legacy environment are acceptable recovery steps.

Official guidance consulted:
- https://learn.chatgpt.com/docs/environments/cloud-environments
- https://learn.chatgpt.com/docs/enterprise/roles-and-workspace-permissions

The cause is unresolved. This report distinguishes browser observations, saved configuration and setup-runtime evidence; it does not assert an ownership defect as confirmed. Private paths, environment/session identifiers, credentials, variable values, screenshots and full transcripts are omitted from this public report.

items.title: Code Review: reply to public PR review summary fails with generic GitHub error

labels.name: bug
labels.description: Something isn't working

labels.name: code-review
labels.description: Issues relating to code reviews performed by codex

labels.name: app
labels.description: Issues related to the Codex desktop app

items.body:
### What version of the Codex App are you using (From “About Codex” dialog)?

`26.1007.21159` (read from the installed application's `CFBundleShortVersionString`). The installed application is named `ChatGPT.app`, bundle identifier `com.openai.codex`. Bundled Code Review plugin: `26.1007.21159`.

### What subscription do you have?

Not recorded during this investigation. The observed error was a GitHub request failure, not a usage-limit message.

### What platform is your computer?

macOS `26.7.1` (build `25G241`), Apple Silicon.

`uname -mprs`: `Darwin 25.6.0 arm64 arm`.

### What issue are you seeing?

In the desktop app's Code Review UI, replying to a review summary on a public pull request fails with:

```text
GitHub could not complete the request
```

The draft remains visible, but the UI does not explain the underlying failure or provide an actionable next step. During read-only diagnosis, the proposed reply was absent from the GitHub PR discussion.

Affected PR: https://github.com/apache/iceberg/pull/18392

Original review: https://github.com/apache/iceberg/pull/18392#pullrequestreview-5478175487

The original review is an approval by `GGraziadei`. The attempted reply quoted the review's two non-blocking nits and added:

```text
Good feedback. Both fixed now.
```

Observed on October 10, 2026. This is a report of the observed failure, not a claim that it has been reproduced across accounts or builds.

### What steps can reproduce the bug?

These are the steps that led to the reported failure:

1. Open Code Review in the desktop ChatGPT/Codex app using the connected GitHub account.
2. Open `apache/iceberg#18392`.
3. Find `GGraziadei`'s approval review and open its reply composer.
4. Quote the review text and enter the reply above.
5. Click **Reply**.
6. Observe `GitHub could not complete the request`; the reply is not posted.

The investigation did not retry the write, to avoid accidentally publishing the comment or creating a duplicate. Consequently, the exact upstream HTTP status, response body, and request ID were not captured.

### What is the expected behavior?

- If the account and connector permit the operation, publish the comment and show the persisted result.
- If the operation is not permitted, preserve the draft and explain which authorization or repository-access requirement is missing.
- If it fails for another reason, show a useful, appropriately sanitized error and a diagnostic/request ID instead of only the generic GitHub message.

### Additional information

#### Verified observations

- The PR was open and unlocked when inspected. The local GitHub CLI was authenticated as `DengYiping`, the PR author. This establishes local authentication, **not** the effective identity or write permissions of the Code Review cloud request.
- Both the local GitHub API and the connected GitHub service could read the PR discussion. Successful public reads do **not** establish permission to post.
- GitHub GraphQL identified the original item as a `PullRequestReview`, not an inline `PullRequestReviewComment`. That review had zero inline comments, and the PR had zero inline review threads at the time of inspection.
- Inspection of the installed Code Review UI and bundled server found that review-summary replies without a review-thread ID take the ordinary PR-comment path. There was no evidence establishing that this case was incorrectly sent as an inline-thread reply.
- The installed UI's GitHub comment capability is derived from write-service availability rather than a demonstrated repository-specific comment permission. This explains why an available Reply button alone cannot establish that the connector can perform the write; it does not by itself prove the permission check is defective.

#### Suspected explanation — NOT confirmed

A connector/repository write-permission mismatch is one possible explanation. The connected GitHub installation lookup returned the personal account and one unrelated organization, but did not include `apache`.

**That installation list is only a clue. It does not prove the effective token, authorization decision, or cause of this failed request.** It remains unconfirmed whether this was an expected GitHub permission rejection surfaced poorly, a bug in the connector/backend, or another upstream failure. No specific HTTP status (such as 403), token defect, or required installation change is claimed.

Please investigate the actual request/response and token permissions before assigning a root cause. Useful coverage would include replying to review summaries on public repositories outside the connected installation scope, and distinguishing ordinary PR comments from inline-thread replies.

Related but not established to have the same cause: https://github.com/openai/codex/issues/49387 (desktop Code Review cloud/local authentication-source selection).

No account connections, permissions, credentials, or application settings were changed during diagnosis. No PR comment was sent by the diagnostic agent.

#### Screenshot

![Failed Code Review reply showing the preserved draft and “GitHub could not complete the request”](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/566b4798-e9ab-4e6b-a780-d2e73f88c677)

labels.description: New feature or request

labels.name: iOS
labels.description: Issues related to the Codex iOS app

labels.name: subagent
labels.description: Issues involving subagents or multi-agent features

items.body:
On the iPhone mobile view of a desktop-connected conversation, a completed subagent leaves a persistent "1 Agent" button directly above the message composer. Opening it shows the subagent as completed, but there is no visible dismiss or hide control. The button stays visible during later messages, including while the keyboard is open.

Steps observed:
1. A conversation spawns one subagent.
2. The subagent finishes and is listed under completed agents.
3. Continue using the parent conversation on an iPhone.
4. The "1 Agent" button remains above the composer with no apparent way to remove it.

Expected: allow users to dismiss completed-agent UI while retaining history, or automatically hide the composer badge when there are no active agents. A label should distinguish completed history from running agents.

Actual: completed work continues to occupy the mobile composer area. This is very frustrating, especially when the subagent was created unintentionally. Starting another conversation is not a satisfactory workaround because the current conversation contains ongoing work.

Please add a visible dismissal control for the completed-agent badge and panel. If this already exists, document how to use it on mobile.

Observed on 10 October 2026. Mobile app/build and iOS version are not confirmed. Private conversation contents, session logs and screenshots are intentionally omitted.

items.body:
### What version of the Codex App are you using (From “About Codex” dialog)?

26.1007.21434

### What subscription do you have?

ChatGPT Plus

### What platform is your computer?

Windows

### What issue are you seeing?

Codex Desktop recognizes available browser backends but cannot successfully interact with Chrome or Edge tabs.

The primary error is:

nodeRepl.fetch request failed

The Codex in-app browser also fails with:

js execution timed out; kernel reset, rerun your request

### What steps can reproduce the bug?

1. Launch the Codex desktop app on Windows.
2. Open Google Chrome or Microsoft Edge and navigate to https://example.com/.
3. Ask Codex to inspect the currently open browser tab and read its title or URL.
4. Codex recognizes the browser backends, but fails to retrieve the tab state with the error: `nodeRepl.fetch request failed`.
5. Run `await cua.listBrowsers()` in the Codex browser automation environment. Chrome, Edge, and the Codex in-app browser are listed.
6. Run `await cua.getState()`. Chrome and Edge return `nodeRepl.fetch request failed`.
7. Attempt to use the Codex in-app browser. The operation may time out with `js execution timed out; kernel reset, rerun your request`.

The issue persists after restarting Windows, updating Codex, and testing both `elevated` and `unelevated` Windows sandbox configurations.

### What is the expected behavior?

Codex should successfully connect to supported browsers (Google Chrome and Microsoft Edge), access open tabs, and read webpage information such as the page title, URL, and content without errors.

The Codex in-app browser should also be able to open webpages and interact with them normally, without connection failures or execution timeouts.

### Additional information

**Additional diagnostic information:**

- The issue affects both Google Chrome and Microsoft Edge.
- The Codex in-app browser also experiences execution timeouts.
- Basic Node REPL execution works correctly. For example, `console.log(1 + 1)` returns `2`.
- `await cua.listBrowsers()` successfully lists Chrome, Edge, Codex In-app Browser, and Codex MCP Apps.
- However, `await cua.getState()` fails to retrieve Chrome and Edge browser states, returning `nodeRepl.fetch request failed`.
- Windows PowerShell confirms that Chrome, Edge, Codex, Node, and Node REPL processes are running.
- Codex session logs contain the following error strings:
  - `nodeRepl.fetch request failed`
  - `helper_unknown_error`
  - `setup refresh had errors`
  - `os error 32`
  - `js execution timed out`
- Some of these errors appear in actual tool-output records, although their exact relationship to the browser failure is not yet confirmed.

**Troubleshooting already attempted:**

- Restarted Windows.
- Updated Codex to the latest available version.
- Tested both Chrome and Edge.
- Tested the Codex in-app browser.
- Tested Windows sandbox settings `elevated` and `unelevated`.
- Verified that basic Node REPL and PowerShell commands work.

None of these attempts resolved the issue.

This may be related to Windows browser-helper initialization, sandbox isolation, or communication between the Node REPL runtime and browser service, but the root cause is unknown.

A potentially related issue is #51601.

I can provide sanitized diagnostic logs if needed.

items.body:
## Environment
- Windows x64; system modules report build 26100.
- Installed desktop package: OpenAI.Codex 26.1007.2314.0.
- Active sandbox helper: %USERPROFILE%\.codex\packages\app-server-daemon\releases\0.162.1-x86_64-pc-windows-msvc\codex-resources\codex-windows-sandbox-setup.exe
- workspace-write, restricted filesystem; local workspace under Documents.
- CUA runtime: %LOCALAPPDATA%\OpenAI\Codex\runtimes\cua_node\cfb32733c877621e.

## Failure
Every tested local shell operation fails before PowerShell starts:
```
Failed to create unified exec process
helper_unknown_error: setup refresh had errors
```
Minimal read-only tests included Get-Location and Get-ChildItem.

Sandbox log:
```
runtime read/execute validation failed:
validate runtime read/execute access on <CUA_RUNTIME>\bin\node_repl.exe:
open ACL target for root-only update:
The process cannot access the file because it is being used by another process. (os error 32)
setup refresh completed with errors
setup error: setup refresh had errors
```
The log also reports a nonfatal sharing violation while granting a non-inheriting read-attributes ACE on the user profile.

## Troubleshooting and observed progression
Repeated application and full Windows restarts did not restore execution.
Stopping the exact node_repl.exe process resulted in its recreation by node.exe running @oai/cua-repl/bin/cua-repl.mjs.
Stopping that verified supervisor and its children moved the fatal validation failure to:
```
<CUA_RUNTIME>\bin\node_modules\@oai\sky\bin\windows\swift\x64\VCRUNTIME140_1.dll
```
Process Explorer search for that DLL returned no results; the holder is unconfirmed.
A subsequent test again failed on node_repl.exe. No project files, ACLs, ownership, runtime binaries, or sandbox settings were modified.

## Process Monitor evidence
Failing process: codex-windows-sandbox-setup.exe, PID 2496, medium integrity.
Captured sequence on the exact DLL path:
1. CloseFile → SUCCESS
2. CreateFile → SHARING VIOLATION
   - Desired Access: Read Attributes, Synchronize, Maximum Allowed
   - Disposition: Open
   - Options: Synchronous IO Non-Alert
   - ShareMode: Read, Write, Delete
3. CreateFile → SUCCESS
   - Desired Access: Read Attributes, Synchronize
   - Disposition: Open
   - Options: Synchronous IO Non-Alert, Open Reparse Point
   - ShareMode: Read, Write, Delete

## Related fix and request
This behavior matches the access-mask conflict addressed by #51822. The published rust-v0.162.1 acl.rs still uses MAXIMUM_ALLOWED in the root-only update branch.

Please confirm the supported desktop/app-server-daemon release containing #51822 and a supported way to update the active helper while preserving local data and sandbox protections. The installed desktop package version alone has not restored execution.

Personal paths have been anonymized. Evidence transcribed from locally collected sandbox logs and Process Monitor; no full diagnostic archive attached.

### What version of the Codex App are you using (From “About Codex” dialog)?

Not collected. This report concerns the desktop app; the cloud runtime version is not being substituted for the desktop app version.

### What subscription do you have?

Not collected.

### What platform is your computer?

Codex desktop app. Desktop OS and OS version were not collected.

### What issue are you seeing?

An existing cloud-backed Codex chat cannot be kept individually pinned. The user reports that choosing Pin briefly moves the chat into Pinned, then it immediately returns to its original sidebar section.

Two attempts through the app's `move_thread_to_sidebar_section` tool also failed with the exact response:

> The task could not be moved into the pinned section.

Fresh `list_threads` checks after the attempts returned the affected chat in `threads`, absent from `pinnedThreads`.

The containing project is pinned, but the chat itself remains unpinned. Other cloud-backed chats already appear in Pinned in the same sidebar.

### What steps can reproduce the bug?

Observed on an existing affected chat; this has not been reduced to a clean-account reproduction.

1. Find an existing cloud-backed Codex chat belonging to a pinned project.
2. Choose Pin in the desktop sidebar.
3. The user reports that the chat briefly enters Pinned, then immediately returns to its original section.
4. Separately, list chats through the app tools and confirm the affected chat is returned as unpinned, with `hostId: "durable"` and `status: "active"`.
5. Call `move_thread_to_sidebar_section` with the returned chat ID, `source: "codex"`, `sectionId: "pinned"`, and `hostId: "durable"`.
6. The tool returns the error quoted above. A fresh list confirms the chat remains unpinned.
7. Retry the same move while omitting the optional `hostId`. The same error occurs, and a subsequent list again confirms the chat remains unpinned.

### What is the expected behavior?

Pinning an accessible chat should leave it individually pinned. If pinning cannot be completed, the app should show a useful explanation rather than briefly moving the chat and then reverting it.

### Additional information

- Observed October 10, 2026.
- Sidebar grouping was by project; chat and pinned sorting were `updated_at`.
- The chat was active during the tool checks. Whether activity, project membership, or cloud backing contributes to the failure is unknown.
- The visual bounce-back is user-reported. The tool failures and readbacks were directly observed by the assistant. A shared underlying cause has not been established.
- Related: #52305 describes pinning failures for Dot-initiated chats; #52510 describes a searchable ChatGPT project conversation not appearing in Pinned. This report concerns a cloud-backed Codex chat, and no shared cause is asserted.
- No desktop logs, screen recording, or in-app feedback ID were collected.
- Private chat titles, project names, thread IDs, and conversation content are omitted.

items.body:
## Summary

In the Codex view of the Windows desktop app, the **`+` icon previously displayed at the far right of the global `New chat` sidebar row is no longer visible**. The right-hand area of that row is blank.

This report is specifically about the **global New chat row at the top of the sidebar**, **not** the separate `+` action beside individual projects.

## Environment

- Product: Codex / ChatGPT Windows desktop application (standalone app, **not** the VS Code extension)
- Version shown in **About Codex**: **26.1007.21434**
- OS: Windows (exact OS build not collected)
- Observed: October 10, 2026
- The missing icon is visible in screenshots of the sidebar in both Chinese (`新聊天`) and English (`New chat`) UI.

## Steps to reproduce (observed on the affected installation)

1. Open the Windows desktop app and switch to **Codex**.
2. Expand the left sidebar.
3. Locate the **New chat** row near the top.
4. Look at the space to the **right** of the New chat text, where the `+` icon was previously shown.
5. The `+` icon is absent; the space remains blank.

## Expected behavior

The global New chat row should show its previous right-hand `+` affordance (unless this was an intentional design change, in which case clarification would help).

## Actual behavior

The `+` icon is not rendered/visible. **Creating chats is still functional**:

- Clicking anywhere on the **New chat** row opens a new chat successfully.
- **Ctrl+N** also opens a new chat successfully.

Thus, this appears to be an **icon visibility / UI-layout regression**, not a failure of the new-chat backend or action itself.

## Troubleshooting already completed

- Restarted Windows: **no change**.
- Used the Windows installed-app **Repair** action: **no change**.
- Rechecked the sidebar afterward: right-hand `+` is still missing.

No app-data reset, cache wipe, or deletion of local Codex settings/history was performed.

## Impact

The disappearance of the familiar `+` control makes the new-chat entry point less discoverable and can initially look like chat creation is broken, even though clicking the row and the keyboard shortcut work.

## Related but distinct reports

- #46250: project-row new-chat buttons missing on pointer hover (different sidebar location).
- #46820: project-level `+` missing (different sidebar location).

Please clarify whether removal of the global New chat row's right-hand `+` is **intentional** in this Windows release, or fix its visibility if unintended. A screenshot of the blank area is available from the reporter.

items.body:
### What version of the Codex App are you using (From “About Codex” dialog)?

26.1007.21159

### What subscription do you have?

ChatGPT Pro 20x

### What platform is your computer?

Darwin 27.0.0 arm64 arm

### What issue are you seeing?

## Description

Codex Desktop consistently reports the following error across all available models on my personal ChatGPT Pro account:

`Selected model is at capacity. Please try a different model.`

However, another personal ChatGPT account works normally on the **same Mac, network, and Codex Desktop installation**.

The affected account has its full usage allowance available and Codex Web works normally.

The issue persisted for several days, temporarily resolved for approximately one day, and then returned.

## Steps to Reproduce

1. Open Codex Desktop and sign in with the affected Pro account.
2. Start a new conversation and submit a simple prompt, such as `Reply with OK`.
3. Observe the capacity error across all available models.
4. Switch to another personal ChatGPT account in the same desktop application.
5. Submit the same prompt.
6. The second account works normally.

## Expected Behavior

Codex Desktop should process requests normally when the account has available usage allowance.

## Actual Behavior

All models fail on the affected account while another account works on the same machine.

Neither account belongs to a managed Business, Enterprise, or Edu workspace.

## Relevant Logs

Previous logs showed:

```text
WebSocket was closed before the connection was established
closeCode=1006
SSH: codex path probe timed out after 60000ms
app_server_connection.connection_failed_before_ready
app_server_connection.reconnect_failed
```

Repeated connection failures were observed, although their relationship to the capacity error has not been confirmed.

## Feedback Upload Issue

I attempted to submit in-app feedback including diagnostic logs.

Feedback ID:

`01a12321-cbc7-7e12-8fd5-320a3534087a`

However, Codex Desktop displayed:

> Feedback upload not confirmed. We couldn't confirm whether your feedback was received. It may have been delivered, and resubmitting could create a duplicate.

Therefore, the feedback upload status remains unknown.

## Additional Information

- Codex Desktop version: 26.1007.21159
- Subscription: ChatGPT Pro
- Usage: Full allowance available
- Both accounts: Personal accounts
- Codex Web: Working on the affected account
- Failure pattern: Recovered for approximately one day, then recurred
- Switching models: Does not resolve the issue

Please investigate whether this is related to account-specific model access, backend request admission, routing, authentication state, or execution-environment problems.

Thank you.

### What steps can reproduce the bug?

### Steps to Reproduce

1. Open Codex Desktop version `26.1007.21159` on macOS.
2. Sign in with my affected personal ChatGPT Pro account.
3. Start a new conversation.
4. Select any available model.
5. Enter a simple prompt:

   `Reply with OK`

6. Submit the request.
7. Codex Desktop returns:

   `Selected model is at capacity. Please try a different model.`

8. Repeat with other available models and new conversations. The same error occurs.
9. Sign out and switch to a different personal ChatGPT account on the exact same Mac, network, and Codex Desktop installation.
10. Submit the same prompt. The second account works normally.
11. Switch back to the affected account. The capacity error occurs again.

### Reproducibility

- The issue has occurred repeatedly over several days.
- It temporarily resolved for approximately one day before recurring.
- All available models are affected on the original account.
- The affected account works normally in Codex Web.
- Neither account belongs to a managed Business, Enterprise, or Edu workspace.

### Session / Feedback Information

- Feedback ID: `01a12321-cbc7-7e12-8fd5-320a3534087a`
- Feedback upload status: Unconfirmed by Codex Desktop.
- Usage allowance: Fully available; no usage limit reached.
- Token limit usage: Not available.
- Context window usage: Not available. The error also occurs in newly created conversations with a minimal prompt.

No special code or repository setup is required to reproduce this issue. A simple text prompt is sufficient.

### What is the expected behavior?

Codex Desktop should successfully process prompts and generate responses using the available models when the account has sufficient usage allowance.

Both personal ChatGPT accounts should be able to use Codex Desktop normally under the same device and network conditions.

For example, submitting `Reply with OK` in a new conversation should return a response rather than a model capacity error.

The affected account should behave consistently with its working Codex Web access and the other functioning account.

### Additional information

### Environment

- Codex Desktop version: `26.1007.21159`
- Operating system: macOS
- Subscription: ChatGPT Pro
- Workspace: Personal account (no managed workspace)
- Usage allowance: Fully available
- Codex Web: Working normally
- Another personal account on the same Mac: Working normally

### Relevant Diagnostic Logs

Previous Codex Desktop logs showed:

```text
WebSocket was closed before the connection was established
closeCode=1006
SSH: codex path probe timed out after 60000ms
app_server_connection.connection_failed_before_ready
app_server_connection.reconnect_failed
```

These logs indicate repeated connection failures. However, I cannot confirm whether they directly caused the model capacity error.

### Feedback Upload Issue

I attempted to submit in-app feedback including logs.

Feedback ID:

`01a12321-cbc7-7e12-8fd5-320a3534087a`

Codex Desktop displayed:

> Feedback upload not confirmed. We couldn't confirm whether your feedback was received. It may have been delivered, and resubmitting could create a duplicate.

The diagnostic upload therefore remains unconfirmed.

### Important Observations

- The problem follows the affected account rather than the computer.
- Switching to another personal account immediately allows Codex Desktop to work normally.
- The affected account has full usage allowance.
- The affected account can use Codex Web normally.
- The problem recovered for approximately one day, then returned.
- The issue affects every available model, not just one model.

### Investigation Request

Could the engineering team investigate possible account-specific model access restrictions, request admission or routing problems, desktop authentication issues, or account-associated execution environment failures?

The controlled comparison between two personal accounts suggests that a general device-wide network or installation issue is less likely.

Thank you.

items.title: ChatGPT for Windows: dot read/send to selected local thread still fail after update (UNKNOWN / NOT_FOUND)

labels.name: bug
labels.description: Something isn't working

labels.name: windows-os
labels.description: Issues related to Codex on Windows systems

labels.name: app
labels.description: Issues related to the Codex desktop app

labels.name: app-server
labels.description: Issues involving app server protocol or interfaces

labels.name: dots
labels.description: Issues involving setting up ChatGPT dots or managing their ongoing work.

items.body:
## Summary

After updating ChatGPT for Windows, I still cannot use my dot to continue the existing local thread selected below. This post-update timing is my observation; a causal regression from the update has not been established.

## Fresh reproduction on October 10, 2026

My dot could not send a harmless `Hola.` message to the existing local Codex thread I explicitly selected. The send returned `CloudThreadNotFoundError` / `NOT_FOUND`. Reading the same thread separately returned `AppServerBackendRequestError: thread not found` / `UNKNOWN`.

The selected computer was reported connected, attached, and authorized for tasks. This records the failure for this particular target through the tools exposed to my dot; it does not establish that all local threads are inaccessible.

## Environment and target

- Desktop product: **ChatGPT for Windows**, as shown in the installed app manifest and Start menu.
- Installed application package version: **26.1007.2314.0**; package identity remains `OpenAI.Codex`.
- Operating system: **Windows 11 Home Single Language, 26H2, build 26300.9550, x64**.
- These installed desktop/package/OS details were checked locally at approximately **2026-10-10 13:54:25 UTC**.
- Executable: `app/ChatGPT.exe`, file version `155.0.8059.40`. This executable file version is included separately and is not the application package version.
- Caller for the dot conversation: ChatGPT web on Windows (`web/windows`).
- Target: an existing thread supplied by me with `hostId=local`.
- Thread ID: `019f4f04-fbfc-7e00-b570-9008d9f558bd`.
- Original target reference: `thread://019f4f04-fbfc-7e00-b570-9008d9f558bd?hostId=local`.
- Browser version and subscription: not captured in this reproduction. Codex CLI version was not queried; this report concerns the ChatGPT desktop/local-thread workflow.
- The thread's contents and current local run state could not be independently verified through the failing dot-side read.

## Observed sequence

1. I supplied the exact local-thread reference to my dot and explicitly asked it to send `Hola.` and report the resulting error.
2. At approximately **2026-10-10 13:51:12–13:51:15 UTC**, the dot called `cloud_threads.send_message` for that exact thread ID.
3. The tool returned the send error shown below, without an admitted turn ID or successful-delivery receipt.
4. At approximately **2026-10-10 13:51:39 UTC**, `cloud_threads.list_environments` reported these fields for the selected computer:
   ```json
   {
     "status": "connected",
     "attached": true,
     "is_authorized_for_tasks": true
   }
   ```
   This is a relevant-field excerpt; computer name, environment ID, and unrelated entries are omitted.
5. A separate `cloud_threads.read` request for the same thread returned the read error below.

### Send request

Tool: `mcp__codex_apps__cloud_threads_send_message`

```json
{
  "threadId": "019f4f04-fbfc-7e00-b570-9008d9f558bd",
  "prompt": "Hola."
}
```

Complete returned send payload:

```json
{
  "content": [
    {
      "type": "text",
      "text": "CloudThreadNotFoundError: The cloud thread was not found."
    }
  ],
  "structuredContent": {
    "error": "CloudThreadNotFoundError: The cloud thread was not found.",
    "error_code": "NOT_FOUND",
    "error_data": {
      "type": "cloud_thread_not_found"
    }
  },
  "isError": true
}
```

### Read request

Tool: `mcp__codex_apps__cloud_threads_read`

```json
{
  "threadId": "019f4f04-fbfc-7e00-b570-9008d9f558bd",
  "limit": 1
}
```

Complete returned read payload:

```json
{
  "content": [
    {
      "type": "text",
      "text": "AppServerBackendRequestError: thread not found: 019f4f04-fbfc-7e00-b570-9008d9f558bd"
    }
  ],
  "structuredContent": {
    "error": "AppServerBackendRequestError: thread not found: 019f4f04-fbfc-7e00-b570-9008d9f558bd",
    "error_code": "UNKNOWN"
  },
  "isError": true
}
```

## Diagnostics and limits

- These are two different operations and error payloads: send returns `NOT_FOUND`; read returns `UNKNOWN`.
- No stack trace, stack frames, server logs, HTTP status, backend request ID, or delivery receipt was included in these returned payloads. The JSON above is the complete error evidence available from those calls.
- The exposed send schema accepts `threadId`, `prompt`, and optional model/thinking settings. It does not expose a `hostId` or `environmentId` parameter. The `hostId=local` part of the supplied reference therefore was not passed as an unsupported argument.
- Inspection of the real dot session's available tool catalog found no `send_message_to_thread` tool or singular `mcp__codex_app__` namespace. This is a tool-catalog observation, not a claim that a native desktop method was invoked and failed.
- Some other delegated tasks have worked in this workflow. They were not rerun as controls in this reproduction, and their success does not establish that this particular existing local target is supported.
- Routing, target eligibility, or task visibility could be involved, but the returned errors do not establish a root cause.

## Expected behavior and requested investigation

An explicitly selected, eligible existing local Codex thread on the connected computer should accept the authorized follow-up through a supported dot-side operation. If this target is ineligible or requires a different route, the response should identify that boundary and the supported next step.

The [October 5–9 release notes](https://learn.chatgpt.com/docs/whats-new/dots-october-9-2026) describe following up on existing Codex threads. The [existing-local-task documentation](https://learn.chatgpt.com/docs/dots/tasks-and-memory#assigned-work) describes continuation on a connected computer, while also noting that connection alone does not grant access to every conversation.

Please clarify which existing local thread types are supported, how the dot should address this target, and how to obtain useful diagnostics when read and send return the errors above.

## Related reports

- #52222: the closest matching Windows dot-to-existing-local-thread send failure.
- #50171 and #49729: related read/send failures, with placement-format errors on read rather than this reproduction's plain `thread not found`.
- #49482: native continuation succeeded in another setup; this is why no universal lack of local-thread support is asserted here.

The target identifier and harmless test prompt are included at my request for tracing. Private project contents, machine/environment identifiers, credentials, and unrelated conversation data are omitted.

labels.name: bug
labels.description: Something isn't working

labels.name: app
labels.description: Issues related to the Codex desktop app

labels.name: session
labels.description: Issues involving session (thread) management, resuming, forking, naming, archiving

items.body:
### What version of the Codex App are you using (From “About Codex” dialog)?

26.1007.21434

### What subscription do you have?

Pro

### What platform is your computer?

Linux 7.2.9-arch1-1 x86_64

### What issue are you seeing?

When switching between existing conversations in the ChatGPT/Codex desktop app on Arch Linux, the selected conversation intermittently fails to render and displays a generic error screen ("ChatGPT hit a snag").

The desktop application itself does not crash or exit. It remains responsive, and reloading fixes it temporarily.

The application logs show a React error boundary being triggered:

```
2026-10-09T21:54:43.858Z
error [electron-message-handler] error boundary
errorName=Error
errorMessage="Missing parent scope"
name=AppRoutes
```

The beginning of the recorded component stack is:

```
at ult (app-shared-2d77298f0100.js:294:139438)
at Y (pinned-6434d8b7b5a1.js:1:1713)
at J (pinned-6434d8b7b5a1.js:1:680)
at Suspense
```

The issue has persisted across application updates and was present before I switched from the `chatgpt-desktop` package to `chatgpt-bin`.

Inspection of the distributed JavaScript identifies the condition that throws this exception. Technical details are included in the Additional information field.

### What steps can reproduce the bug?

1. Launch the desktop application on Arch Linux.
2. Open an existing conversation.
3. Navigate between existing conversations using the sidebar.
4. Intermittently, the selected conversation displays the error screen instead of its content.
5. Switch to another conversation. The application remains functional and the newly selected conversation loads.

**Reproducibility:** Intermittent. I can reproduce the failure during normal conversation navigation, but have not yet identified a deterministic sequence or a minimal reproduction case.

No specific prompt or code execution is required to trigger the observed failure.

### What is the expected behavior?

Switching between existing conversations should consistently render the selected conversation without triggering a React error boundary.

Navigation should preserve the required UI scope/context hierarchy. An error in one conversation view should not make that view unusable.

### Additional information

## Environment

- OS: Arch Linux
- Kernel: 7.2.9-arch1-1
- Architecture: x86_64
- Desktop session: Wayland
- Application package: `chatgpt-bin 26.1007.21434-1`
- Previous package: `chatgpt-desktop`
- The package change was an attempted workaround for an already-existing issue. It did not resolve the problem.

## Investigation of bundled JavaScript

I inspected the minified JavaScript distributed with the application inside `/usr/lib/chatgpt/resources/app.asar`.

This is an analysis of the distributed application code, not the original unminified source.

### 1. Exception originates in the shared scope provider

In `app-shared-2d77298f0100.js`, the function `ult` contains:

```javascript
a = t.parent == null ? void 0 : r.get(t.parent.id)
```

It then checks:

```javascript
if (t.parent != null && a == null)
    throw Error("Missing parent scope");
```

The exception is thrown when a scope declares a parent, but that parent cannot be found in the current scope context.

### 2. The component stack leads to TabThumbnailScope

The `Y` component in `pinned-6434d8b7b5a1.js` renders a scope provider:

```javascript
jsx(u, {
    scope: ne,
    value: N,
    children: R
})
```

The value `N` is constructed using a `dndId`.

Tracing the imported symbol `ne` through `app-initial-ed5807835d97.js` identifies the scope definition:

```javascript
Enr = _l("TabThumbnailScope", {
    parent: ps
})
```

### 3. The parent resolves to RouteScope

The imported `ps` symbol resolves to `g1` in `app-shared-2d77298f0100.js`, defined as:

```javascript
g1 = sO("RouteScope", {
    key: fEr,
    parent: pY,
    retain: {max: 20}
})
```

This establishes that `TabThumbnailScope` requires `RouteScope` as its parent.

## Interpretation

The exception and component stack indicate that the affected UI tree attempts to render a scope provider without its required parent being registered in the current scope context.

This is consistent with the observed failure during navigation between conversations.

**The precise underlying cause is not yet established.** In particular, I have not confirmed whether this is caused by component remounting, retained view state, incorrect provider nesting, or a lifecycle race.

The `pinned-*.js` bundle name should not be interpreted as evidence that user-pinned conversations are responsible.

## Additional diagnostics

The failing log entry occurred on October 9, 2026, at 21:54:43 UTC.

I can provide further redacted application logs or additional source-level findings if useful.
