items.body:
### What version of the Codex App are you using (From “About Codex” dialog)?

codex-cli 0.162.1

### What subscription do you have?

ChatGPT Pro

### What platform is your computer?

Microsoft Windows NT 10.0.26200.0 x64

### What issue are you seeing?

# apply_patch treats a numeric hunk header as literal context

I am reporting a reproducible parser diagnostic and an instruction-compatibility
problem in Codex. I am not assuming that support for standard unified-diff hunk
headers is promised by the custom apply_patch format.

## Environment

- Reproduced on 2026-10-08, native Windows, PowerShell 7.6.6.
- Installed Codex CLI version: 0.161.0.
- Actual failing interface: tools.apply_patch invoked inside functions.exec.
- The PATH apply_patch.bat belongs to the installed OpenAI Codex package and
  invokes codex.exe with --codex-run-as-apply-patch. The CLI launcher itself was
  not tested for this report; CLI equivalence is not claimed.

## Minimal reproduction without access to my project

The attached fixture.txt and control.patch contain synthetic text only. Extract
them into a fresh disposable directory and open that directory as a Codex
workspace. No original repository, credentials, network service or private data
are needed.

fixture.txt is UTF-8 without BOM, LF line endings, and a final newline:

```text
first
second
third
```

Ask Codex to submit the following exact patch to its built-in apply_patch tool.
Set the Update File path to the fixture.txt in your disposable workspace. An
absolute path may be used when required by the host; preserve the numeric hunk.

```text
*** Begin Patch
*** Update File: fixture.txt
@@ -1,3 +1,4 @@
 first
+inserted
 second
 third
*** End Patch
```

Observed response, with only the workspace path redacted:

```text
apply_patch verification failed: Failed to find context '-1,3 +1,4 @@' in <workspace>\fixture.txt
```

The fixture remains unchanged. Its SHA-256 was identical before and after:

```text
f5c962601b413ccda2fc14d64d98479d9fc74c90c2dde15f25ee9922e57f5074
```

The intended change is simply to insert the line inserted between first and
second. The equivalent standard unified diff in control.patch has the same
numeric hunk range. The read-only command below actually ran and returned exit
code 0, with the fixture still unchanged:

```powershell
git apply --check control.patch
```

This verifies the standard unified representation only. The custom Begin Patch
and Update File envelope is not a standard unified diff. The control patch was
not applied. No bare-@@ control was executed on the fixture.

## Why this blocked an authorized edit

Our local instructions require both:

```text
Use apply_patch for edits.
Hunk headers must contain ranges, such as @@ -12,3 +12,4 @@.
Bare @@ is prohibited.
After a failure, stop, reread the file and diff, and prepare a new focused patch.
```

The numeric form fails in the parser. In the original session, automatic
approval review also rejected attempts without numeric ranges because they
violated those local instructions. These are separate failure modes: an
approval rejection does not prove that the parser ran. The approval behavior
depends on host/policy configuration and has not been independently reproduced
in a fresh support session.

To reproduce the instruction conflict, provide the instructions above in a new
Codex session and request the one-line insertion using apply_patch with a
numeric hunk header. Do not grant permission to bypass approval rejections.

## Requested investigation

OpenAI's Apply Patch documentation describes V4A and shows bare @@ markers:
https://developers.openai.com/api/docs/guides/tools-apply-patch

Please confirm the intended supported format for this Codex tool. If numeric
unified-diff hunks are intentionally unsupported, please return an explicit
unsupported-format diagnostic instead of searching for the header as file
content. Codex should also identify incompatible local instructions early and
explain the format mismatch accurately, instead of cycling between parser
errors, prohibited patch variants and approval requests.

No tracked project file was modified by this reproduction. The synthetic
fixture, its hash, the failing call and the successful read-only Git check are
the verified evidence; support for another format remains a question.


### What steps can reproduce the bug?

[](url)

[control.patch](https://github.com/user-attachments/files/33283250/control.patch)
[FEEDBACK.md](https://github.com/user-attachments/files/33283252/FEEDBACK.md)
[fixture.txt](https://github.com/user-attachments/files/33283251/fixture.txt)

### What is the expected behavior?

_No response_

items.title: Codex Diff reports reverted transient edits as final changes and inflates file/line counts

labels.name: bug
labels.description: Something isn't working

labels.name: extension
labels.description: Issues related to the VS Code extension

items.body:
## Summary

The VS Code Codex Diff panel can present transient edits that were later reverted as if they were part of the final workspace diff. This materially inflates the reported file and line counts and disagrees with both VS Code Source Control and Git.

In one completed local task, Codex Diff reported:

- 42 files changed
- +922 / -2515 lines

The actual final repository state reported by both `git status` and `git diff` was:

- 25 files changed
- +381 / -165 lines
- no staged files
- no untracked files
- no assume-unchanged or skip-worktree entries
- no submodules

## Concrete example

Codex Diff displayed this file as `+93 / -420`:

`rust/crates/mediabox-tv/src/screens/media_settings.rs`

The displayed right-hand side contained an intermediate cleanup, including removal of `PlayerChoice` and large deletions elsewhere in the file. That candidate edit had been reverted before task completion.

At completion, the file was byte-for-byte identical to HEAD:

```text
git diff --exit-code -- rust/crates/mediabox-tv/src/screens/media_settings.rs
exit=0

worktree hash: 746d28397c461778a4957ac1af2f408ca6a3a8d7
HEAD hash:     746d28397c461778a4957ac1af2f408ca6a3a8d7
```

The same HEAD-identical result was verified for at least these additional files that Codex Diff still presented as changed:

- `rust/crates/mediabox-tv/src/detail.rs`
- `rust/crates/mediabox-tv/src/input.rs`
- `rust/crates/mediabox-tv/src/platform.rs`
- `rust/crates/mediabox-tv/src/prefs.rs`
- `rust/crates/mediabox-tv/src/rpc.rs`
- `rust/crates/mediabox-tv/src/screens/account.rs`
- `rust/crates/mediabox-tv/src/screens/audio.rs`
- `rust/crates/mediabox-tv/src/screens/discover.rs`
- `rust/crates/mediabox-tv/src/screens/ethernet.rs`
- `rust/crates/mediabox-tv/src/screens/library.rs`
- `rust/crates/mediabox-tv/src/screens/media.rs`

## Steps that appear to trigger it

1. Start a Codex task in a Git repository.
2. Let the agent edit a group of files.
3. Revert or replace some of those candidate edits during the same task.
4. Finish the task.
5. Compare the Codex Diff panel and its “files edited” summary with:
   - VS Code Source Control
   - `git status --short --untracked-files=all`
   - `git diff --shortstat`
   - `git diff --name-only`
6. Codex Diff may retain the reverted intermediate edits and count them as final work.

## Expected behavior

Codex Diff and the completion summary should describe the final reviewable state, or clearly label a separate view as cumulative session activity that includes reverted edits.

A file that is identical to HEAD must not be presented as a current code change. Reverted edits must not inflate the “files edited” or added/deleted line totals.

## Actual behavior and impact

The panel presented a historical intermediate patch as final work. This made it appear that hundreds of additional lines and 17 additional files had been changed when they had not.

This is especially serious in an agent UI because users rely on the diff to audit what the agent actually delivered. The mismatch can make undone work appear completed and is materially misleading even when the underlying snippets were once written temporarily.

## Requested response from OpenAI

The affected user explicitly requests a response from OpenAI about:

1. whether Codex Diff is intended to show final workspace state or cumulative session activity;
2. why reverted/HEAD-identical files were presented as final changes;
3. whether file and line totals shown in the completion UI can currently be relied upon;
4. the planned remediation or tracking status for this issue.

Please respond on this issue so the reporter receives the update through the linked GitHub account's notification settings.

## Environment

- VS Code: 1.141.0 (`2a59476c9bfcb90b3ddc372c36762471b7dfad1c`), x64
- OpenAI Codex extension: `openai.chatgpt@26.1007.21434`
- Codex Audio extension: `openai.codex-audio@26.1007.21434`
- OS: Linux 7.2.9-2-cachyos x86_64
- Git: 2.56.0

Two screenshots showing the 42-vs-25 mismatch and the false `+93/-420` per-file diff are available if maintainers need them. Repository content, username, and user-identifying local paths are intentionally omitted from this public report.

items.title: Preserve pre-exec subagent effort defaults when parent overrides follow exec

labels.name: bug
labels.description: Something isn't working

labels.name: exec
labels.description: Issues related to the `codex exec` subcommand

labels.name: CLI
labels.description: Issues related to the Codex CLI

labels.name: subagent
labels.description: Issues involving subagents or multi-agent features

labels.name: config
labels.description: Issues involving config.toml, config keys, config merging, or config updates

items.body:
### What version of Codex CLI is running?

`codex-cli 0.162.1`, npm-installed Linux x64 native binary. `npm view @openai/codex version` also returned `0.162.1` on 2026-10-10.

### What subscription do you have?

ChatGPT authentication; subscription tier not collected.

### Which model were you using?

`gpt-6.1-sol`. Every parent rollout recorded `high`; children inherited this model without a model override.

### What platform is your computer?

Linux 6.8.0-146-generic x86_64 GNU/Linux; Debian 13 development container.

### What terminal emulator and version are you using (if applicable)?

Noninteractive `exec`, stdin/stdout redirected. Environment reports VS Code 1.140.0; no interactive terminal was needed for the reproduction.

### Codex doctor report

Native `codex doctor --json` was run. Redacted summary: version 0.162.1; installation/config/auth/provider HTTP and WebSocket checks OK; background app-server not running; latest npm version matches installed version. Overall warning was nine stale rollout DB rows in the normal user home. The reproduction used a separate empty temporary Codex home, not that normal-home state. This diagnostic describes the normal installation, not the clean experimental home; no remediation was applied. Unrelated personal paths and historical session inventory are omitted.

### What issue are you seeing?

An unnamed native child ignores the configured `agents.default_subagent_reasoning_effort="medium"` and runs at its parent's `high` effort when the child-default `-c` appears before `exec`, while the parent model/effort options appear after `exec`.

Moving the same settings to the same side of `exec` restores the expected behavior. The clean native-binary comparison reproduced both outcomes twice. Explicit per-spawn `reasoning_effort: "xhigh"` worked in every case.

| Option placement | Parent recorded effort | Unnamed child | Explicit xhigh child | Runs |
|---|---|---|---|---:|
| Child default + model/parent effort before `exec` | high | medium | xhigh | 2 |
| Child default before; model/parent effort after `exec` | high | **high** | xhigh | 2 |
| Child default + model/parent effort after `exec` | high | medium | xhigh | 1 |

The last control moved only the child-default override from before to after `exec`; the parent model/effort options stayed after `exec`. This is observable native CLI behavior; the internal cause has not been established.

The impact is unexpected child effort and associated cost/latency behavior, with no visible rejection of the configured default. A launcher that supplies defaults before the subcommand can encounter this when a caller supplies parent options after it.

### What steps can reproduce the bug?

Use the installed **native binary directly**, not a custom launcher. For the tested clean controls, `CODEX_HOME` was an empty temporary directory with only an `auth.json` symlink to the existing authenticated home (no credentials copied). Working directory was an empty temporary directory. `--ignore-user-config`, `--ignore-rules`, and `--no-daemon` were used. No custom configuration, global AGENTS file, custom role files, memory, hooks, or custom skills were supplied in that home. Native prompt rendering was inspected independently to confirm the custom instructions/skill catalog were absent.

Use the same prompt file in all three cases:

```text
Codex-native effort acceptance probe only. Make no filesystem changes and use no shell, web, MCP, consult, or review tools. Spawn exactly two default-role children sequentially using the native spawn_agent tool. Both receive exactly: Reply only PROBE_OK; do not use tools or delegate. First: task_name unnamed_effort, fork_turns none, omit reasoning_effort and omit model entirely. Wait for completion. Second: task_name named_effort, fork_turns none, reasoning_effort xhigh, omit model entirely. Wait for completion. Do not set an explicit medium level for the unnamed case: its omission is what this experiment measures. Report only the two returned child identifiers and their completion. No additional spawns or retries. The orchestrator will inspect native rollout turn_context records for effective model and effort. Task explicitly authorizes these two native child probes; children may not delegate. This is not a review or consultation.
```

Below, `$CODEX_BIN` denotes the absolute path to that native binary. Run from the empty temporary working directory with the clean `CODEX_HOME` already selected.

Passing control (both settings before `exec`):

```sh
"$CODEX_BIN" --no-daemon -m gpt-6.1-sol \
  -c 'model_reasoning_effort="high"' \
  -c 'agents.default_subagent_reasoning_effort="medium"' \
  -c 'project_doc_max_bytes=0' \
  -c 'features.multi_agent=true' \
  -c 'features.hooks=false' \
  -c 'features.memories=false' \
  -c 'web_search="disabled"' \
  -c 'sandbox_mode="read-only"' \
  exec --ignore-user-config --ignore-rules --skip-git-repo-check --json - < prompt.txt
```

Failing case (child default before; model/parent effort after `exec`):

```sh
"$CODEX_BIN" --no-daemon \
  -c 'agents.default_subagent_reasoning_effort="medium"' \
  -c 'project_doc_max_bytes=0' \
  -c 'features.multi_agent=true' \
  -c 'features.hooks=false' \
  -c 'features.memories=false' \
  -c 'web_search="disabled"' \
  -c 'sandbox_mode="read-only"' \
  exec -m gpt-6.1-sol -c 'model_reasoning_effort="high"' \
  --ignore-user-config --ignore-rules --skip-git-repo-check --json - < prompt.txt
```

Passing recovery control: take the failing command and move **only** `-c 'agents.default_subagent_reasoning_effort="medium"'` after `exec`; leave the parent model/effort options there as well.

Inspect the parent rollout's actual spawn arguments and each child's `session_meta` parent linkage and `turn_context` effort. These observations came from persisted runtime records, not the models' self-reports. The first spawn actually omitted `reasoning_effort` and `model`; the second named `xhigh`. All children completed successfully. Do not use `--ephemeral` if checking these persisted records.

Clean-control thread bindings:

| Case | Parent | Unnamed child | Recorded child effort |
|---|---|---|---|
| Both before, run 1 | `01a12601-b943-7db0-8d42-5db9950ce6fb` | `01a12601-d00f-7000-a776-95fb4169eccc` | medium |
| Both before, run 2 | `01a12607-0e18-7d21-9884-2e9656234b81` | `01a12607-254d-7521-af6a-0b94cc7180fc` | medium |
| Split, run 1 | `01a12606-8b07-7652-8db6-0390c75ea787` | `01a12606-9d64-7a10-a53d-53d7174db702` | high |
| Split, run 2 | `01a12607-52a8-7d62-92f9-36f858fd888d` | `01a12607-620e-7b62-a808-f9143d295d4d` | high |
| Move only child default after | `01a12608-0eb3-7fc1-9a51-00402562f997` | `01a12608-26e5-7b31-a8f6-7bf44741783c` | medium |

### What is the expected behavior?

An unnamed child should use the configured medium default independently of the parent's high effort, whether valid CLI overrides are placed before or after `exec`. An explicit child `xhigh` override should continue to take precedence. Settings for different keys should not disappear based on subcommand placement.

### Additional information

- Related: #39012 reports a pre-/post-subcommand override drop for `app-server` on 0.147.0. This report covers native `exec` on current 0.162.1 and demonstrates the resulting child-effort behavior. It may share a cause, but no parser-level causal claim is made here.
- #33881 concerns registered agent TOML pins; the clean reproduction here has no custom agent TOML.
- The first comparison moves model and parent-effort options together; it does not independently attribute the problem to either option. The final control isolates moving the child-default override alone.
- `rust-v0.162.1` source for `cli/src/main.rs` prepends root overrides into exec overrides, and `core/src/agent/child_config.rs` applies the default subagent effort when omitted. Source inspection alone did not explain the observed discrepancy.
- Additional custom-setup controls disabled project documents, memories, hooks, changed sandbox mode, and changed cwd without fixing the split-placement failure. Custom hooks/instructions are not required to reproduce it.
- Full redacted measurements and comparison evidence: https://github.com/MTin3D/codex-config/issues/122#issuecomment-6098074877
- No live configuration, provider configuration, or other running session was changed. Disposable clean-home histories were summarized into the linked evidence before cleanup; thread IDs above identify those measured records, not histories uploaded to this report.

### What issue are you seeing?

# Feedback: `apply_patch` did not honor the selected worktree

## Summary

In a repository with multiple Git worktrees, the patch-editing interface wrote
to the primary shared worktree instead of the explicitly selected external
worktree. This can put unrelated work at risk when multiple agents or users
work concurrently.

## Environment

- Windows host, PowerShell shell
- One Git repository with a primary worktree and a separately created external
  worktree on a feature branch
- Multi-agent session with a shared filesystem

## Steps to reproduce

1. Start in a Git repository whose primary worktree is on `develop`.
2. Create a separate worktree at another absolute path and check out a feature
   branch there.
3. Request an edit using the patch-editing interface while the task's selected
   working directory is the external worktree.
4. Inspect `git status` in both worktrees.

## Expected result

The patch is applied only in the selected external worktree. The primary
worktree remains unchanged.

## Actual result

The edit appeared in the primary shared worktree. The external worktree stayed
clean. The discrepancy was detected before further edits, so no unrelated work
was overwritten.

## Impact

This is especially risky when:

- another agent owns changes in the primary worktree;
- a user intentionally isolates work on a feature branch; or
- an agent assumes the patch tool follows its command working directory.

It can lead to edits being committed from the wrong branch or colliding with
parallel work.

## Safe workaround used

Before continuing, verify `git status` and branch identity in both worktrees.
If the external worktree is clean and the changes are known to be only the
current task's edits, remove the unused external worktree and switch the
primary checkout to the intended feature branch. Do not continue editing until
the destination is unambiguous.

## Requested behavior

Make the patch-editing interface honor the active task worktree / selected
working directory, or expose an explicit target-worktree parameter. If that is
not possible, fail safely when multiple worktrees exist instead of silently
editing the primary worktree.

items.body:
## Summary

I am a ChatGPT Plus user reporting a persistent Codex / ChatGPT Work reliability problem that began on **September 24, 2026** and has remained unresolved across both:

- **Codex Desktop on macOS**
- **ChatGPT Work / Codex on the web**

This is not a report about one long conversation or one isolated failed task. The failures have occurred across multiple separate conversations, including newly created / low-context conversations.

I am **not asserting a root cause**. I am asking OpenAI to correlate the existing diagnostics and determine whether this is a client, account/session, cloud-task recovery, streaming/session, usage-accounting, or other service-side issue.

The primary impact is that Codex / Work is not reliable enough for normal paid production use.

The usage observation described below is **not the primary complaint**. It is relevant because, while the underlying Codex/Work reliability problem remains unresolved, I cannot reliably distinguish normal intentional usage from usage associated with failed requests, retries, background/cloud activity, interrupted tasks, or accounting delay.

---

## Impact

Since Sep 24, I have repeatedly had to abandon or recreate Work/Codex conversations because an existing conversation became unusable.

Observed effects include:

- work interrupted after substantial progress;
- conversations becoming inaccessible;
- cloud tasks appearing to continue while the front-end stream/conversation becomes unavailable;
- repeated retries / reconnects;
- inability to know whether usage consumed during failure periods represents normal model work or failed/background activity.

My first priority is **restoring stable Codex / Work operation**.

Usage correction is secondary and should be reviewed after the underlying service problem is understood.

---

## Timeline

All times below are **UTC+8** unless otherwise stated.

### Sep 24, 2026 — Codex Desktop failures begin

The same Codex Desktop workflow/setup had been working normally before this date.

Beginning Sep 24, multiple separate Codex Desktop conversations started showing failures including:

- `{"detail":"Bad Request"}`
- `Reconnecting 5/5`

Important observations:

- failures occurred in multiple short/new conversations, not only in a long-context thread;
- in one conversation, even simple text messages produced three consecutive `Bad Request` failures;
- one affected conversation later recovered temporarily, then failed again while Codex was still processing, without a new user message causing the transition;
- quitting and reopening Codex Desktop did not reliably resolve the issue.

### Sep 24–25 — Diagnostics captured

I captured and submitted:

- Codex Desktop logs covering Sep 24–25;
- a Codex feedback/session identifier;
- exact affected conversation identifiers;
- screenshots and timestamps.

I am intentionally **not posting raw logs, conversation UUIDs, support-case identifiers, account information, or local user paths publicly**. These can be provided privately to OpenAI maintainers for correlation.

### After approximately Sep 26 — Desktop largely removed from the workflow

After the Desktop failures, I stopped intentionally running Codex Desktop production tasks and moved primarily to **Work/Codex on the web**.

This matters because later failures were not limited to the original Desktop environment.

### Oct 3, 2026 ~02:07 — Fresh Work web conversation fails

A newly created Work web conversation with very little context failed with:

- `Could not load this ChatGPT conversation`

This was not a large legacy thread and did not require a complex external workload before the failure appeared.

### Subsequent Work web failures

Across separate Work conversations I observed combinations of:

- `Could not load this ChatGPT conversation`
- `Unable to send this ChatGPT message`
- `Unable to check locked mode`
- `A network error occurred. Please check your connection and try again.`
- `Resume stream unavailable`
- connection interruption while waiting for a complete response
- conversation becoming inaccessible while cloud work appeared to remain active

Standard ChatGPT remained usable during at least some of the same periods when Work/Codex was failing.

### Oct 7, 2026 ~22:56 — Cloud Work reaches 99%, then disconnects

A Work task running in the cloud reached **99%** and then the conversation showed a connection interruption / waiting-for-complete-response state.

The task had already performed substantial work before the stream/session failed.

### Oct 8, 2026 ~00:42–00:48 — Temporary recovery, then another stream failure

The same general Work session recovered temporarily and became usable again, then failed again with:

- `Error in message stream`

My last known intentional ChatGPT / Work activity before the later usage observation was approximately **Oct 8 around 00:48 UTC+8**.

### Oct 10, 2026 ~20:31 — Usage present before any new task/message

This is the clearest usage-related observation.

Before this moment:

- the Mac had been powered off for approximately **2+ days**;
- I had not been using Codex Desktop or ChatGPT Work;
- I had not opened ChatGPT on the web;
- when I powered on the Mac, I had not opened Chrome yet;
- I had not sent any Codex message;
- I had not started any Codex/Work task;
- I do not use this OpenAI account on another device during this period.

I opened Codex Desktop only to check the allowance/reset time.

Before sending any message or starting any task, the UI showed:

- **5-hour allowance: 98% remaining (2% used)**
- approximately **01:06 remaining until reset** in the captured screenshot

OpenAI support later confirmed that the screenshot matched the account-side state they could see and also stated that **simply launching Codex Desktop is not expected to start a new five-hour window**.

Support suggested possible explanations such as prior usage already counted in the window, a cloud/background task continuing or retrying, or reporting/accounting delay, but email support stated that it could not access the per-event ledger needed to identify the exact event.

I am not claiming which explanation is correct.

I am asking for the exact account/service-side event to be correlated with this observation.

---

## Expected behavior

1. Codex / Work conversations should remain accessible while a task is running and after it completes.
2. A transient stream failure should not make an in-progress or completed cloud task effectively unreachable.
3. New/short conversations should not repeatedly fail with `Bad Request`, reconnect exhaustion, or conversation-load errors.
4. If a Work/Codex task continues in the cloud after the front-end connection is lost, the UI should reliably recover the task state and provide a clear stop/control path.
5. Work/Codex usage should be attributable to understandable user-initiated or documented background activity.
6. Merely opening Codex Desktop before sending the first message should not itself create unexplained usage.

---

## Actual behavior

The failure mode is intermittent and can temporarily recover, then return.

Across Desktop and web I have observed:

- request rejection (`Bad Request`);
- repeated reconnect exhaustion;
- conversation-load failure;
- unrecoverable / unavailable response streams;
- Work cloud execution progressing while the conversation UI becomes disconnected or inaccessible;
- temporary recovery followed by another failure;
- unexplained Work/Codex usage present before a new user message/task after a long inactive period.

This combination makes it difficult to determine whether a failed UI/session represents:

- a client-only stream failure;
- a server-side conversation/session problem;
- an orphaned/retrying cloud task;
- delayed usage reporting;
- or another backend state issue.

---

## Important controls / observations

These points are included to avoid repeating explanations that do not fit all observed cases:

- The failures are **not limited to one long conversation**.
- At least one failure occurred in a **new / very low-context Work conversation**.
- The problem is **not limited to Codex Desktop**; it also occurred in Work on the web.
- After approximately Sep 26, I was no longer intentionally running Desktop Codex production tasks, yet web Work failures continued.
- Some failures occurred after a task had already made substantial cloud progress.
- Standard ChatGPT remained usable during some Work/Codex failures.
- The Oct 10 usage observation occurred before Chrome was opened and before any new Codex message/task was started.
- I am not claiming that all of these symptoms necessarily have one root cause; I am asking OpenAI to correlate them.

---

## Diagnostics already available to OpenAI

I have already collected/submitted:

- Codex Desktop logs for Sep 24–25;
- exact affected Desktop conversation IDs;
- exact affected Work web conversation IDs;
- a Codex feedback/session ID;
- screenshots of the error states;
- timestamps for the failures;
- the Oct 10 usage screenshot.

For privacy/security, I am **not publishing those unique identifiers or raw logs in this public issue**.

I can provide them privately to an OpenAI maintainer/engineer who can correlate them with backend telemetry.

---

## Possibly related public reports

I am not claiming these issues have the same root cause. These are included only because parts of their observed symptoms overlap:

- #48393 — ChatGPT Web/Android: intermittent conversation-load failures and 429-style errors during Sep 24–26
- #50000 — Codex Desktop: existing conversations intermittently fail to load while Work may still appear active

items.body:
### What variant of Codex are you using?

ChatGPT dot with Work/Codex cloud and connected-computer tasks, alongside ordinary ChatGPT chats and Projects.

### What feature would you like to see?

I want to use my dot as my chief of staff across all my projects. I want to be able to grant it broad, owner-controlled permissions so it can organize and coordinate my existing work without making me copy context between chats or start over in a new thread.

Please provide a supported account-wide orchestration interface covering ordinary ChatGPT chats and Projects, cloud Work/Codex tasks, and eligible existing local threads on my connected computers.

The capabilities I need are:

1. **Find and understand existing work.** Discover my chats, projects and tasks; read the conversations, files and project instructions I authorize; and keep the source and project boundaries clear.
2. **Continue existing conversations.** Send an instruction or follow-up into the correct existing chat or task, receive its response, and coordinate the next step. Searching or reading a conversation alone is not enough.
3. **Manage project organization.** Create chats and projects; choose the correct project when starting work; and move, rename, archive or delete eligible chats/projects with explicit permissions, appropriate confirmations and recovery options.
4. **Coordinate across execution environments.** Delegate work to the appropriate supported cloud or connected-computer environment, preserve the right project context, track progress and blockers, and bring results back to my main dot conversation. Existing local threads should be supported where compatible, with clear explanations when they are not.
5. **Work across devices.** Let me direct this from my phone as well as desktop/web, with usable links, status and results. The interface should make it clear when a connected computer must be online.
6. **Choose models and delegation where supported.** Let me select a model or authorize appropriate model/worker selection, with visible capability, usage and cost limits.

**Permissions and control**

I would like an explicit opt-in for broad access to my own account, plus granular controls by project, conversation, action and connected computer. Permissions should be inspectable and revocable, with exclusions and an audit trail showing what was read, changed, delegated or sent where. Archive/restore and undo should be available where possible, with clear confirmation for irreversible deletion. Existing safeguards for sensitive data, external sharing, credentials and consequential actions should still apply.

**Example workflow**

From my phone, I ask: "Review my active projects, continue the existing conversation for this task, delegate the implementation to my connected computer, keep everything in the right project, and bring me the result or any decision you need."

I should be able to approve that scope once through a clear permission flow and then see the authorized work progress without repeatedly pasting transcripts, locating thread IDs or manually moving conversations.

### Additional information

I searched the existing issues. Related requests cover pieces of this workflow:

- #29275: visible child-thread creation in Codex Desktop
- #32519: shared ChatGPT–Codex project context and bidirectional handoff
- #50042 and #50144: dot integration with ChatGPT Projects
- #52564: persistent project-level supervision of Codex threads

The specific request here is a single, owner-authorized dot workflow across **existing ordinary ChatGPT conversations, project lifecycle management, and both local and cloud task execution**, including permission controls for continuing and organizing that work.

My existing reports #50697 and #50698 concern specific desktop/local-thread failures. This feature request is separate from those bug fixes. Some individual capabilities may already exist; the request is for a documented, reliable end-to-end experience rather than a claim that every component is missing.

If cross-product parts belong to another OpenAI team, please route this feedback to the relevant team.

### Screenshots

The following screenshots are from the original report #51956 and illustrate the reported behavior:

items.body:
### What issue are you seeing?

Summary
I’m trying to use dot to access existing Codex threads that I created myself, rather than tasks originally created by dot. Reading these threads fails with backend errors, even though my Windows desktop is connected and dot can discover my local Codex projects.
This appears inconsistent with the recently announced ability to follow up on existing Codex threads:
Official announcement:
https://x.com/ChatGPT/status/2108636748217770180?s=20
Official release notes:
https://learn.chatgpt.com/docs/whats-new/dots-october-9-2026
Related documentation:
https://learn.chatgpt.com/docs/dots/tasks-and-memory
The announcement describes starting Codex work and following up on existing threads. In my tests, access works for a previously dot-created task, but fails for the user-created threads tested below.

### What steps can reproduce the bug?

Environment
- Test date: October 10, 2026; earlier attempts also failed before this date.
- Codex/ChatGPT desktop on Windows; requests to dot sent through ChatGPT web on Windows.
- Desktop reported connected, attached, and authorized for tasks.
- I updated the desktop app and requested another test. The same Architect-thread error persisted afterward.
- Reconnecting the computer did not resolve that error either.
- Exact desktop app/build version was not captured during these tests.
Steps to reproduce
1. Connect the Windows desktop to dot.
2. Copy a codex://threads/<thread_id> link from an existing user-created Codex session.
3. Ask dot to read that thread without sending messages or modifying it.
4. dot invokes cloud_threads.read with the supplied threadId and a small limit, such as 2 or 3.
5. The request fails before returning conversation content.
Tools used
- cloud_threads.read — full tool name: mcp__codex_apps__cloud_threads_read.
- cloud_threads.list_threads with children_only=false, limit=50; archived=true was checked separately.
- cloud_threads.list_environments.
- cloud_threads.list_projects with the connected computer’s environmentId.
Observed results
A. Existing project-associated Architect thread:
AppServerBackendRequestError: Client specified an invalid argument: post-cutover thread ID <THREAD_A> has unsupported placement format version 2
This was reproduced repeatedly, including after the desktop update and reconnection.
B. Another existing user-created thread:
AppServerBackendRequestError: Client specified an invalid argument: post-cutover thread ID <THREAD_B> has unsupported placement format version 3
C. An existing session not associated with a project:
AppServerBackendRequestError: thread not found: <THREAD_C>
D. A new session I created specifically for testing after the update:
AppServerBackendRequestError: Client specified an invalid argument: post-cutover thread ID <THREAD_D> has unsupported placement region 10
These read failures returned isError=true and error_code=UNKNOWN. No conversation content was returned.
Successful control checks
- cloud_threads.read successfully returned messages from a previously dot-created task on the same computer.
- cloud_threads.list_environments confirmed the desktop connection and task authorization.
- cloud_threads.list_projects successfully returned my registered local projects, including the relevant project’s ID and root path.
Additional findings and limits
- Account-level list_threads returned 30 IDs with no continuation cursor. The first two failing thread IDs were absent. The archived list was empty. This listing check occurred before the new test session was created.
- That listing exposed IDs, not thread titles or project associations. It therefore did not provide a usable list of chats belonging to my local project.
- Project discovery only confirms access to the sidebar project registry. Its registered root path is an old folder; active worktrees are elsewhere. We did not establish access to those worktrees through this check.
- The read-tool description mentions expanded access to existing threads, but no available status field confirmed whether that capability is enabled for my account.
- No messages were sent to the affected threads. No threads or worktrees were created by dot during this investigation, and no project files were changed.
Expected behavior
dot should be able to resolve and read an authorized existing local Codex thread on the connected computer, consistent with the announced feature. If a thread type, account rollout, or app version is unsupported, the error should explain the requirement or limitation clearly.
Impact
I cannot use dot to follow an existing Architect session and coordinate ongoing project work. I still have to manually copy messages and reports between Codex and dot.
Diagnostic interpretation — not a confirmed root cause
The placement-format and placement-region errors suggest a possible thread-ID compatibility or routing problem. We have not confirmed whether this involves local versus cloud thread storage, rollout state, permissions, or another backend issue. The errors do not establish that the threads were deleted, and “region 10” should not be assumed to represent my geographic location.
Please investigate why existing-thread reads fail while desktop/project discovery and a dot-created-thread read succeed, and confirm whether any account setting or client update is required.
I can provide the actual thread IDs privately through Feedback/support; they are intentionally omitted from this public report.

### What is the expected behavior?

items.body:
## Summary

Since approximately mid/late September 2026, a fleet of recurring **ChatGPT Work / Scheduled Tasks on the web** has suffered intermittent connector failures that are strongly **execution-surface dependent**. The owner reports that **manually initiated / interactive workflows generally work with the same connected services**, while unattended scheduled runs intermittently complete research or reads but cannot persist their results. In some cases a small, already-authorized GitHub mutation is stopped by **OpenAI's safety checks before GitHub can respond**; other cases involve different Google Drive/Docs tool/runtime defects.

This affects **multiple connector families, not just GitHub**. The first-hand evidence in this report is specifically **GitHub and Google Drive/Docs**. We do **not** claim every connector has been individually tested or that they all fail with the same error. Independent reports describe comparable scheduled-write authorization symptoms in Gmail, Google Sheets, and Trello (linked below).

**Important scope:** This is about the hosted **ChatGPT Work scheduled/automation execution path**, *not a locally reproduced bug in the open-source Codex CLI or Windows sandbox*. This repository already tracks related ChatGPT Web/automations issues (#48940 and #38350); please route to the owning runtime/connectors team if a different tracker is canonical.

## Environment and scope

- Product: ChatGPT Web / Work; recurring unattended Scheduled Tasks, with separately invoked manual / interactive runs for comparison.
- Operational pattern: approximately **15 enabled hourly agents** across independent projects during the 2026-10-10 investigation. Their recorded last-run timestamps showed invocation, **not** that work completed or was persisted.
- Connected apps investigated: **GitHub** and **Google Drive / native Google Docs**.
- Permission configuration independently checked by the owner: **Allow all actions** for **each** of GitHub and Google Drive. A lower global default for other apps does not override those app-specific settings.
- Repository access and interactive connector writes work in at least some owner-triggered executions (including creation and readback of the public diagnostic issue linked below).
- Exact model, reasoning effort, task-run trace IDs, internal policy decisions and connector/backend builds **are not visible** through the accessible Scheduled-task inspector. There is **no completed controlled model A/B comparison**. We cannot attribute this to “large models” or a particular Codex version.
- Failure is intermittent; neither a successful manual write nor a healthy single scheduled run establishes a permanent fix.

## What actually fails (keep these failure layers separate)

### A. GitHub: authorized writes refused while reads/other writes succeed

Some scheduled jobs can inspect repositories or otherwise run normally but fail to persist by `create_blob`, `create_file`, or `update_file`. Recorded operator/worker reports include the tool-facing message:

```
This tool call was blocked by OpenAI's safety checks.
```

A particularly useful history:
- A scheduled workflow's GitHub `create_blob` operation was blocked, while later work on the same code/repository path succeeded (see [EndlessZen #250, Oct 8 evidence](https://github.com/drevendev/EndlessZen/issues/250#issuecomment-6068892583)).
- A scheduled worker reported `create_file` rejected even though owner-session/interactive GitHub writes had succeeded ([EndlessZen #249, Oct 8 evidence](https://github.com/drevendev/EndlessZen/issues/249#issuecomment-6068830628)).
- This interactive session successfully **created and read back** the related owner-authored investigation issue [EndlessZen #260](https://github.com/drevendev/EndlessZen/issues/260). That verifies a working interactive GitHub write path on Oct 10; it is **not** proof of a byte-identical scheduled-vs-manual test, which remains needed.

A host-side safety refusal is **not** a GitHub HTTP 403, expired OAuth token, or a provider rejection unless the provider was actually called and such a response was captured. For many failures that distinction is invisible to the operator.

### B. Drive/Docs: a different set of failure boundaries

- Google Drive file upload workflows encountered an apparent missing **runtime file-reference / file handoff** even in a non-ledger diagnostic, so the run could not complete an upload ([EndlessZen #250, evidence](https://github.com/drevendev/EndlessZen/issues/250#issuecomment-6023744193)). This is not automatically a Google OAuth failure.
- Native Google Docs positional insertion sometimes **returned success but damaged adjacent text** (e.g. isolated `0` or malformed `+03:000` clock field) when the client guessed a structural insertion index, even with a revision guard ([EndlessZen #250, evidence](https://github.com/drevendev/EndlessZen/issues/250#issuecomment-6023680917)). This is a **corrupt-success / insertion-contract** failure, not proof that the same safety layer caused it.
- Both types prevent reliable persistence and recovery, even if the model's analysis or a prior read succeeds.

### C. Failure amplification and loss of diagnostics

One denied or ambiguous persistence step can make later hourly runs look like “no work”, freeze local agent progress accounting, or cause duplicate writes when the worker guesses whether the previous call took effect. That local accounting deadlock is also an application design defect and **should not be blamed entirely on OpenAI**; our own mitigation is being tracked separately in [EndlessZen #249/#250](https://github.com/drevendev/EndlessZen/issues/260).

Crucially, **a worker whose GitHub/Drive writes are blocked cannot be required to save its own error log to those same systems**. When a tool call is refused before provider dispatch, the model may receive only the generic refusal, not the underlying policy decision or request ID. If the run also fails before returning a result, the operator has no raw error to attach.

## Scheduled vs manual comparison (current strength of evidence)

| Context | Observed outcome | Limitation |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Unattended hourly Work/Scheduled runs | Intermittent refusal at GitHub write or Drive/Docs persistence despite enabled jobs and per-app Allow all actions | Not every run fails; different error classes exist |
| Owner-initiated / interactive workflows | Owner reports normal operation in ordinary manual execution; interactive GitHub issue creation/readback was independently verified | This is **not** yet a controlled identical-payload A/B across all providers |
| Missing run/connector data | A failed external write may leave no durable report and sometimes no exposed low-level error | Absence of a GitHub commit is not itself proof of any particular safety, network, auth or policy layer |

Independent issue [#48940](https://github.com/openai/codex/issues/48940) and its comments contain **stronger exact-payload interactive-vs-scheduled reproductions** for GitHub, including a scheduled `create_file` safety refusal followed by successful interactive creation of the actual previously blocked article payload.

## Suggested reproducible test for OpenAI

1. In a test ChatGPT account, connect GitHub and Google Drive, set **Allow all actions** for both, and choose disposable test destinations with explicit authorization. Verify the current owner/target; do not test with real private content.
2. Create a minimal recurring **Scheduled Task** that first reads and then writes one small deterministic GitHub fixture under a fixed path, followed by readback. A separate scheduled task should create/update a small Drive/Docs fixture with exact readback. Do not depend on one tool to store the other tool's diagnostic.
3. Use the same connector account and **same safe fixture payload** in a manually started workflow. Test scheduled vs manually initiated run explicitly (and ordinary interactive, if these are different surfaces) while controlling for prompt, model when visible, task version, time and file size.
4. Repeat over enough scheduled intervals to catch intermittent outcomes. Preserve a host-owned per-run trace with execution context, tool action, gate type, whether provider dispatch occurred, redacted provider response/request ID, timing, approval state and verified external after-state.
5. Test independent failure classes separately: a refused GitHub mutation, missing upload handoff, and a syntactically successful but semantically corrupted Docs mutation. Do not treat all as “the connector disconnected.”

**Expected:** An authorized, supported connector action should behave consistently between manual and scheduled contexts, or clearly explain a documented policy/scope difference before dispatch. Unattended jobs should never be left indistinguishably “successful” when the requested remote effect did not occur. Generic “safety checks” denials need a concrete, supported remediation/diagnostic reference. Host-owned run diagnostics must not depend on the failed connector.

## Related independent reports (not evidence from our account)

- [openai/codex#48940](https://github.com/openai/codex/issues/48940) — GitHub scheduled write safety refusal; comments include controlled interactive comparisons.
- [openai/codex#38350](https://github.com/openai/codex/issues/38350) — recurring Work tasks become Paused without authorization; a *separate* scheduler-lifecycle problem we have also encountered historically.
- [openai/codex#50769](https://github.com/openai/codex/issues/50769) — authorization-context confusion with Dots/GitHub; related but not an identical surface.
- [openai/codex#52714](https://github.com/openai/codex/issues/52714) — size-dependent GitHub approval despite Allow all actions in a separate controlled test; **our report does not establish that payload size caused our failures**.
- [OpenAI community: cross-provider scheduled safety checks](https://community.openai.com/t/regression-scheduled-tasks-safety-checks-block-authorized-gmail-sends-and-google-sheets-writes/1403242) — independent Gmail/Google Sheets/Trello/GitHub reports, including successful interactive Trello controls.
- [EndlessZen owner-side investigation #260](https://github.com/drevendev/EndlessZen/issues/260) — dated evidence, incident references, local counterexamples, diagnostic taxonomy and mitigations.

### Public incident context, not a single universal diagnosis

OpenAI acknowledged separate incidents during the period, including [Sep 29: tasks could fail to start/resume/finish during a settings-connection exhaustion incident](https://status.openai.com/incidents/01M3Q4RK1SM4EMK445GGPG7C0N/write-up), [Oct 5–6: Work Mode issue affecting scheduled tasks](https://status.openai.com/incidents/01M45E0JFFJZ6EQ3BWYPW74R2Z), and [Oct 9: apps/plugins availability incident](https://status.openai.com/incidents/01M4HA7BCCXVHTR5DCYMSBQF2H). These were individually bounded incidents; **we do not claim they establish a continuous weeks-long outage or explain every failed run**.

## Requested action

1. Confirm which execution-policy, approval and connector-runtime differences exist between **unattended Scheduled** and **manually initiated** ChatGPT Work runs, especially when both are configured with app-level Allow all actions.
2. Investigate false-positive pre-provider GitHub safety blocks and silent/ambiguous app writes; correlate with host traces rather than requiring user-generated logs through the failed path.
3. Provide host-owned redacted run/error diagnostics and an explicit approval/remediation path when user-granted app permission is insufficient.
4. Distinguish actual provider HTTP failures from host policy refusals, missing file-handoff capabilities, corrupt-success document writes, and local agent bookkeeping deadlocks.
5. Route the report to the right **ChatGPT Work/Scheduled/connector** owning team if this is not maintained by the open-source Codex CLI team.

Sanitized public report. No private repository names, credentials, task identifiers, internal document IDs or payloads are included.

labels.name: bug
labels.description: Something isn't working

labels.name: app

items.body:
## Summary

Submitted at the affected user's explicit request after a troubleshooting session on 2026-10-10.

Computer Use can enumerate and activate windows and perform some keyboard actions, but screenshot capture consistently fails. This blocks an authorized end-to-end CapCut editing task, including visual verification and export.

Possibly related to #35446. The matching symptoms do not establish that the exact internal deadlock reported there is the cause on this machine.

## Environment

- OS: Microsoft Windows 10 Pro, version 10.0.19045, x64
- Codex desktop: 26.1007.21434, build 13901, production channel
- Built-in update check: `up_to_date`
- Computer Use plugin: 26.1007.21434
- GPU: NVIDIA GeForce RTX 3060
- GPU driver reported by Windows: 32.0.15.9621
- Display: 1920 x 1080
- Local interactive console session active
- Target application: CapCut 9.4.0.4015

## Reproduction using the supported API

1. Through node_repl, import `sky` from `@oai/sky`.
2. Call `sky.list_windows()` and select the unique returned CapCut window.
3. Call `sky.activate_window({ window })`.
4. Call `sky.get_window_state({ window, include_screenshot: true, include_text: true })`.
5. Refresh window selection and repeat with `include_text: false`.

Observed errors:

```text
FrameArrived timed out: timed out waiting on channel
window capture timed out: timed out waiting on channel
```

Screenshot capture also failed for a normal File Explorer window during the same troubleshooting session. Earlier attempts with OBS also failed, so the symptom is not limited to CapCut.

Accessibility-only requests return a tree, although CapCut exposes mostly unnamed elements. Window activation and some keyboard actions work; a normal Alt+F4 close was verified by subsequent window enumeration. Earlier click attempts reported that coordinate input geometry was unavailable.

## Troubleshooting already performed

- Re-selected current returned window objects instead of using stale handles.
- Activated the target before capture.
- Tried screenshot capture both with and without accessibility text.
- Reset the JavaScript kernel, re-imported the supported API and retried.
- User fully restarted the desktop app; a new app window was observed afterward, but capture still failed.
- Checked that the Windows console session is active.
- CapCut and DWM report responding; the GPU reports status OK.
- Checked selected recent Windows Application/System events and available desktop logs; no specific cause of the capture timeout was established.
- Checked for an eligible desktop update; the updater reports up to date.

No capture-helper binary patch, alternate screenshot backend, security/privacy changes, OS upgrade or GPU-driver change was applied.

## Expected behavior and impact

Computer Use should return a usable screenshot and support reliable subsequent input on this Windows installation, or provide an actionable compatibility error with a supported workaround. Repeated generic timeouts leave the user unable to complete desktop editing through the agent.

Generating CapCut project files outside the UI did not solve the task: without native visual feedback, an initial project had incorrect title sizing and required user screenshots. This is an editing workaround limitation, not evidence of a CapCut bug.

## Request

Please confirm whether this current build is affected by #35446 and provide an official fix or supported workaround. If additional diagnostics are needed, please specify a supported way to collect capture initialization, FrameArrived, bitmap-conversion and result-delivery traces.

This report intentionally excludes personal file paths, screenshots, account identifiers, source media and raw conversation/application logs.

items.title: [Windows Desktop 26.1007.2314.0] Background Git diff mapping interferes with external builds; no independent disable control

labels.name: bug
labels.description: Something isn't working

labels.name: windows-os
labels.description: Issues related to Codex on Windows systems

labels.name: app
labels.description: Issues related to the Codex desktop app

items.body:
## Summary

Codex Desktop on Windows continues to launch background Git diff scans that memory-map tracked build files. External build tools can then fail to delete or overwrite those files. This was observed with desktop version **26.1007.2314.0**.

This is a standalone report of current-version impact on external builds, related to #24681 and #46235. It is not limited to agent patch writes.

## Environment

- Windows, Codex Desktop package version 26.1007.2314.0.
- A local Git repository containing tracked build artifacts.
- The external build task was started manually in an editor.
- Paths, account identifiers, project names, original filenames, and absolute timestamps are intentionally omitted.

## Evidence A: mapping overlaps an external build's deletion failure

Process Monitor captured the following sequence for the same generated binary file. Times are relative to the first successful mapping:

| Relative time | Process / operation | Result |
| --- | --- | --- |
| 0 ms | Codex-launched Git: CreateFileMapping | SUCCESS |
| approximately 266 ms | External PowerShell build script: SetDispositionInformationEx | CANNOT DELETE |
| approximately 492 ms | Same Git process: CreateFileMapping | SUCCESS |
| approximately 941 ms | Same Git process exits | Process Exit |

Captured process ancestry was:

```text
ChatGPT.exe (Codex Desktop)
  -> git.exe
    -> git.exe
```

The mapped file was the same file the external build script attempted to delete. The Git process was still alive at the failed deletion. The observed background command included:

```text
diff --no-ext-diff --no-textconv --color=never
     --find-renames --raw --no-abbrev --numstat
```

These commands were launched by the desktop application, not requested as part of the build.

## Evidence B: a separate build metadata file is also mapped

In another capture, eight Codex-launched Git diff process instances repeatedly created read-only mappings of a tracked build metadata file. Process ancestry again traced back to the Codex desktop executable.

The external build intermittently failed to overwrite that metadata file with:

```text
FileNotFoundException:
The requested operation cannot be performed on a file with a user-mapped section open.
```

The failed metadata write was not captured together with its blocking mapping. This second capture confirms the desktop Git mapping behavior for another build file; it does not independently identify the exact mapping owner at the earlier failed write.

## Workaround attempted

Setting `git-review-mode="last-turn-only"` did not stop background scans.

No usable independent control was found to disable automatic Git diff scanning while keeping the desktop application open.

## Expected behavior

- Keeping Codex open should not interfere with external build tools deleting or overwriting repository files.
- Provide an explicit setting to disable automatic background Git diff scanning while retaining chat and agent functionality.
- A disabled state should stop and cancel scans rather than merely hide the review panel.

## Actual behavior and impact

Background Git diff scanning continues and can overlap external build operations. Users encounter intermittent build failures and must investigate file mappings or close the application.

Please investigate the current desktop implementation and validate against concurrent external writes and deletions, including tracked binary artifacts.

## Related reports

- #24681: background `git diff --numstat` and Windows mapped-section write failures.
- #46235: mapped-section conflicts during patch writes and desktop Git mapping evidence.

This report adds current-version observations and a captured mapping/deletion-failure overlap in an external build.

## Privacy

This report contains anonymized event summaries only. No repository files, screenshots, full traces, local paths, usernames, or conversation transcripts are attached.

items.title: [Escalation] Codex Desktop repeatedly disconnects on long-running sessions (5/5 retries); request engineering ownership review

labels.name: bug
labels.description: Something isn't working

labels.name: windows-os
labels.description: Issues related to Codex on Windows systems

labels.name: app
labels.description: Issues related to the Codex desktop app

labels.name: connectivity
labels.description: Issues involving networking or endpoint connectivity problems (disconnections)

labels.description: Issues involving session (thread) management, resuming, forking, naming, archiving

items.body:
## Formal reliability complaint and request for engineering escalation

Codex Desktop is repeatedly failing during a long-running development project. The user has already tried troubleshooting, and the disruption is preventing normal project completion. Please escalate this to engineering management for review of issue ownership, remediation priority, and the effectiveness of the current fix process.

### Reproduction context
- Windows Codex Desktop (exact version not yet collected)
- ASUS Merlin router with Shadowsocks proxy
- Other Codex conversations on the same connection work normally
- One existing long-running development conversation is disproportionately affected; keeping that conversation and its history intact is a requirement

### Observed failures
- `stream disconnected before completion: Transport error: network error: error decoding response body`
- Occasional unexpected TLS close / EOF
- Automatic retries progress to `5/5` and may still fail
- At other times the session resumes and continues work, then disconnects again at unpredictable points during normal execution, not only during visible context compaction

### Impact
Repeated failures are blocking substantial, long-running software development. Asking the user to start a new conversation sacrifices project continuity and is not an adequate remedy. Repeated manual retries also risk duplicated or partially completed steps.

### Requested action
1. Investigate streaming transport, session resumption, and long-context processing for existing conversations, including how failures are recovered after all retries are exhausted.
2. Preserve the original conversation and project state; provide a supported in-place recovery solution.
3. Escalate recurring reports to engineering management, review ownership/staffing or bring in additional expertise if needed, and communicate a concrete progress update.
4. Provide a way to capture useful, privacy-safe diagnostic logs and correlation identifiers without requiring users to delete conversation history.

This report does not assume the root cause is proven: the long session is correlated with the failures, while router/network and server transport also remain possibilities.

Please avoid closing this solely with generic network-troubleshooting advice without reviewing the session-specific failure pattern.
